Week 12 kicks off with the UCF eyeing a win over Iowa State as slight 1.5-point favorites on Friday, Nov. 20. My Iowa State vs. UCF prediction and college football picks lean toward the Knights' defense keeping the Cyclones' ground attack in check. Kickoff at the Acrisure Bounce House is set for 6 p.m. ET on FS1. Moneyline prediction: UCF Over/Under prediction: Under 49.5 Who will win Iowa State vs UCF: UCF moneyline Screw the points, give me UCF outright on senior night. UCF has been up and down since taking down BYU following the Cougars' upset win over Notre Dame. However, the Knights draw an Iowa State team nearing the end of its first season without Matt Campbell. The Cyclones have leaned on their ground attack all season, running the ball on more than 56% of their plays. However, UCF ranks No. 1 in the Big 12 in fewest explosive rushing plays allowed , per StatRankings . If the Knights can contain the run, they should be able to slow down Iowa State's offense. Interestingly enough, Iowa State has allowed the fourth-fewest explosive passing plays while giving up nearly eight yards per pass attempt and 230 passing yards per game. The Cyclones' defense is surrendering more than 415 total yards per contest, which is a lot of production for a unit that has done a good job limiting big plays. UCF is playable up to 60%. TOP PICK Iowa State vs UCF Over/Under pick: Under 49.5 Orlando is dealing with significant rainfall this week, and the weather could play a major role in Friday night's matchup. AccuWeather has a flood watch in place from Tuesday at 5 p.m. through Friday at 7 p.m., while The Weather Channel is projecting up to an inch of rain Friday night. Slick conditions could make things difficult for both offenses, especially with two teams that have shown a tendency to get off to slow starts. UCF's rushing attack is one of the worst statistical ground games in the country, while Iowa State relies on running the football on more than 56% of its plays. If the Knights can contain the Cyclones' ground attack, they should have a chance to control the tempo and limit explosive plays. Between the weather concerns, two potentially sluggish offenses, and a lack of urgency on either side, I don't mind looking toward the Under here. It hosts another one Friday night when Iowa State blows in. The Knights (5-5, 3-4 in Big 12) last reached the postseason in 2023. UCF vs Iowa State prediction Beating Iowa State is pretty simple: Contain Aiden Flora, and you've got 'em. The third-year sophomore has five games in which he's gone over 100 yards. In those games, his lowest output was 182 yards in a 42-31 defense-optional shootout against Baylor two weeks ago. The Cyclones are 4-0 in those other games, three of which saw Flora surpass 200 yards on the ground. He's racked up a ridiculous 619 yards and six touchdowns over the past three games, adding eight catches for 58 yards as well as a pair of pass completions (only one went for anything, a 37-yarder last week vs. Cincinnati). UCF's run defense ranks eighth in the 16-team Big 12 at just under 137 yards per game. They held Arizona State to 3.6 yards per carry last week but surrendered nearly 5 ypc and four touchdowns to Kansas in a winning effort the week prior. Arkansas State transfer Jaylen Raynor has led the Big 12's worst passing offense at just under 207 yards per game, but even he's played better in recent weeks amid Flora's ascension, throwing for 794 yards and six TDs against just two interceptions. The Knights can absolutely win on Senior Night. The run game was stifled by Arizona State, but UCF was without lead back Duke Watson, and Iowa State has the third-worst run-stopping unit in the Big 12. If everyone is back and healthy, and if Alonza Barnett can complement that with some timely strikes, the Knights can get the win. The Cyclones haven't won any of their four road games this season, but three of those teams (Iowa, BYU and Arizona) are ranked. A bowl berth might come down to the final week, just like it did in 2023. 2026 Week 12 Preview: Iowa State Cyclones @ UCF Knights
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 12 Preview: Iowa State Cyclones @ UCF Knights | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 20, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Big 12 UCF and Iowa State battle for bowl eligibility at the Bounce House, while Aiden Flora is on a hot streak. Time and date: Friday, November 20 at 6:00 p.m. ET Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: UCF (-2.5) Over/under: 49.5 All-time series: Iowa State leads, 1-0 Last meeting: Iowa State 38, UCF 35 — October 19, 2024 Current streak: Iowa State, 1 (2024) Setting the scene Friday night football kicks off early this week. At 6 p.m. ET, the Bounce House welcomes Iowa State for the first time as two 5-5 Big 12 opponents compete for bowl eligibility. UCF has been the master of chaotic finishes this season, recently shocking BYU in double overtime and upending Kansas with a game-winning touchdown on the final snap. Iowa State has also escaped a handful of close finishes this year, sliding past West Virginia in a back-and-forth finish before kicking a game-winning field goal on Halloween to upset Oklahoma State. With two teams accustomed to close finishes chasing that coveted sixth win, and a potential Heisman finisher involved, Friday night in Orlando should feature no shortage of drama. Iowa State Cyclones outlook Iowa State (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) has been as battle-tested as anyone in college football this season. The Cyclones already faced four teams ranked in the top 20 of the latest College Football Playoff rankings. They’ve also defeated three Big 12 opponents with records of 5-5 or greater, eking out close wins over West Virginia and Oklahoma State before blowing the doors of Cincinnati last Saturday. There have been two different versions of the Cyclones in year one under Jimmy Rogers. In Ames, Iowa State is a force to be reckoned with, posting a 5-1 home record with a lone defeat to No. 2 Utah. Yet, the Cyclones remain in search of their first road victory under Rogers, although all four of their road opponents are currently 6-4 or better. Iowa State’s success is largely correlated with the performance of Doak Walker Award semifinalist Aiden Flora. The running back has catapulted into the No. 1 spot on the nation’s rushing leaderboard at 1,335 yards, thanks to three consecutive 180+ yard explosions. Flora has an FBS-best five 180-yard games this year, including three performances where he eclipsed 210 yards. The versatile sophomore is a touchdown machine, and his scoring ability isn’t limited to just the run game. In addition to producing 12 rushing touchdowns, Flora has thrown two passing touchdowns and recorded a punt return touchdown, and he also ranks second on the team in receptions. The explosive Flora has four 60-yard runs this year, a total topped by just three FBS programs. His ability opens up things for the passing game, which has a commensalistic relationship with the future All-Big 12 running back. All three of Jaylen Raynor’s 250-yard showings through the air occurred when Flora crossed 180 on the ground. The mobile quarterback has been able to stretch the field more vertically as of late. He has started 10 games this season, yet 42 percent of his passing yards and 46 percent of his passing touchdowns occurred in the last three weeks. Raynor has established a strong connection with true freshman Jamal Polite Jr., who averages 19.5 yards per reception as the premier downfield threat. But what happens when Flora goes under 180? Iowa State has struggled when it gets behind the sticks. The Cyclones are 113th nationally in third down offense, and Iowa State has converted just 20-of-71 (28.2 percent) third downs across its five losses. The Cyclones have been inconsistent on defense. They enjoyed strong performances against BYU and Cincinnati but allowed at least 39 points in four of their last six contests. Iowa State ranks 108th in total defense, struggling particularly against the run where it allows 174 yards per game on a 4.93 average. Inside linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen has been one of the unit’s key playmakers, checking in at third in the Big 12 with 93 tackles. However, the Cyclones are severely lacking in two categories on defense: sacks and interceptions. They rank 100th in the FBS with 1.6 sacks per game, and defensive end Isaac Terrell leads the unit with 3.5 — producing three of those sacks in the Sept. 5 opener. Additionally, Iowa State has only picked off two passes all season, and two were courtesy of middle linebacker Beau Goodwin. Thus, the secondary looks to make more havoc plays and avoid these high-scoring shootout style games moving forward. UCF Knights outlook UCF (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) is on the brink of its second bowl appearance since joining the Big 12 in 2023. The Knights are the last remaining program that has yet to produce a winning record as a member of the conference, but the opportunity to end the drought presents itself this November. Since stunning then-No. 2 BYU in overtime on Oct. 24, the Knights are 0-2 at home, dropping lopsided contests to Baylor and Arizona State. All four of UCF’s Big 12 losses came by at least 10 points, while all three wins were by single-digits, as the Knights have shown the ability to prosper in tightly-contested games. To qualify for bowl eligibility, UCF must jumpstart its offense which has scored 22 points across its last two games at the Bounce House. The Knights recently returned to their original starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III, who suffered a hamstring injury in Week 2 at Pittsburgh. Barnett has won 13 of his last 16 starts, and the senior has elevated the passing attack, surpassing 250 passing yards in both starts this November. Barnett’s presence on the field has turned wide receiver Josh Derry into a budding star. In his past two games, Derry has hauled in 15 receptions for 280 yards and a touchdown, emerging as the top receiver in this offense. True freshman Tyren Hornes is also making strides, registering 59 receiving yards (his second-highest total of the season) and his second career touchdown against the Sun Devils. However, the Knights must improve their pass protection, as they rank 113th nationally with 2.7 sacks allowed per game. That correlates to an unsatisfying third down conversion rate of 34.4 percent, which sits one spot below Iowa State on the national leaderboard. But perhaps the greatest struggle for UCF’s offense — which is also related to the offensive line — is the decline of the run game. The Knights haven’t produced a 100-yard rusher since Week 3, or a 60-yard rusher in each of their last three games. No UCF running back has rattled off a 20-yard run since Oct. 24, and the Knights look to create lanes for Duke Watson, Landen Chambers, and Taevion Swint to break that streak. The Knights are typically strong starters on defense, and they have yet to allow more than seven points in a first quarter this season. However, finishing games is a priority for a unit that allowed 25 unanswered in the final 20 minutes against Kansas and 27 unanswered in the final 20 minutes against Houston. UCF continues to operate without one of its top defenders in strong safety Demari Henderson, who suffered an injury late in the BYU game on Oct. 24. Still, there is veteran talent across the secondary including cornerback Antione Jackson, whose 10 pass breakups lead the Big 12, and cornerback Jayden Williams, who ranks second on the team with 53 tackles, in addition to recording one interception and two forced fumbles. While the Knights are better than the Cyclones in turnover production, they similarly struggle in getting to opposing quarterbacks. Defensive end Isaiah Nixon leads UCF with 2.5 sacks on the season, and the team has gone consecutive weeks without registering a sack. Despite the offenses trending in different directions, UCF opens as a slight favorite over Iowa State, largely due to the location of the game. The Knights recorded two of their three Big 12 wins at the Bounce House, while the Cyclones have been futile away from home this year. The plamayking of Aiden Flora will be the main determinant in this matchup. Flora recorded over 100 rushing yards and three touchdowns in the first quarter last week, almost single-handedly putting Cincinnati away in 15 minutes. UCF’s defense must be prepared to counter the running back in any way possible. Stacking the box isn’t always an ideal strategy, because Iowa State loves to catch defenses off-guard with his pop passes. The Cyclones will keep things creative on offense, and UCF must remain disciplined defensively beyond the first quarter. Iowa State sustains its offensive rhythm from the last three weeks, while the Knights struggle to find openings for their run game. The end result: the Cyclones become bowl eligible in Jimmy Rogers’ debut season. The Knights are 1.5-point home favorites in a matchup between two teams looking to secure bowl eligibility. Iowa State enters the game following a dominant 41-13 victory over Cincinnati, led by Aiden Flora's 216 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Meanwhile, UCF is coming off a disappointing 26-13 loss to Arizona State. The Cyclones have struggled away from home this season, while the Knights have been much more competitive in Orlando. Kickoff is scheduled for 5:00 p.m. CT on FS1. Below, we'll break down the latest Iowa State vs. UCF odds, where to watch, key injuries and expected starters, along with our prediction and pick for this Friday night Big 12 showdown. Jenkins was listed as a game-time decision ahead of the Arizona State game, making his availability an important storyline heading into Friday. UCF running back Duke Watson was listed as unavailable against Arizona State, while Iowa State quarterback Connor Moberly was also listed as out against Cincinnati. The official Big 12 availability report for this matchup has not yet been released. This section will be updated as additional injury information becomes available. Iowa State vs. UCF Biggest Question: Who Stops the Run? Both teams would like to try and establish the run. Iowa State is led by star running back Aiden Flora, while UCF has a more balanced approach to the running attack, led by Duke Watson. Iowa State's offense has been far superior this season, ranking No. 28 in the country in yards per play, while UCF's offense is outside of the Top 100. However, it's UCF's defense that ranks in the Top 60 in yards per play, while Iowa State is outside the Top 100. Whoever wins this battle will have the leg up in this game on Friday night. I also don't want to overreact to their huge performance vs. Cincinnati last week. A road game on a Friday night is a much toughest spot. That being the case, UCF just hasn't earned my money in this spot, or the right to be a favorite. And it feels like the offense has either taken a step back, or just gotten confused since it had to move to back to Alonza Barnett at QB compared to where it was with Keyone Jenkins. UCF is last in the Big 12 in first downs and 15th in third-down conversions. And while Iowa State's defense hasn't been great, they've also played some of the most explosive offenses in the Big 12, like Utah, Arizona and Oklahoma State. picks.blurb: Iowa State-UCF Prediction: Can The Cyclones Battle Through The Rain? IowaStateRoundtable 17 Members • 197 Posts IowaStateRoundtable IowaStateRoundtable Related stories Trending stories IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Iowa State-UCF Prediction: Can The Cyclones Battle Through The Rain? Brad Schultz Partner Nov 19, 2026 3:17 AM Published Nov 19, 2026 3:17 AM This matchup between 5-5 teams should be an all-out fight for bowl eligibility. Here's how Publisher Brad Schultz sees this one playing out. More Videos No one expected Iowa State football to be in the position it's in right now, and why would they? Jimmy Rogers had to rebuild this Cyclone program from the ground up after Matt Campbell left for Penn State and gutted the roster in the process. Some programs can endure such a teardown and instantly be in the national spotlight the following season, but few thought it could be done at Iowa State, one of the losingest Power Four college football programs. While it's certainly not all cupcakes and rainbows in Ames right now, the Cyclones currently sit at 5-5 – one win away from an improbable trip to a bowl game. But there's no time for Iowa State to celebrate just yet. It has two games to finish the job and get at least one win to secure bowl eligibility and continue its sudden momentum. The first game on the docket takes place on Friday against UCF. The Knights are also 5-5, so this matchup has the potential to be an all-out war in what looks to be soggy Florida weather in Orlando. Related stories More content will be coming out on Thursday, but in the meantime, here's how I see this matchup playing out. Matchup: Iowa State Cyclones (5-5, 3-4) @ UCF Knights (5-5, 3-4) Location: Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando, Florida Scheduled game time: Nov. 20 at 5 p.m. CDT Weather: 72 degrees with rain (flash flood warning have been issued) Announcers: Noah Reed (play-by-play) and Petros Papadakis (analyst) Radio: Cyclone Radio Network (John Walters, Eric Heft) Betting information (as of Nov. 18 and per DraftKings): UCF -2.5 | O/U: 48.5 As I've been saying all week, I feel like this is an extremely winnable game for Iowa State. While UCF does boast a really good win over BYU, the Knights have been extremely inconsistent under Scott Frost (who folks in the state of Iowa should know by now). They've alternated wins and losses since the dramatic win over the Cougars on Oct. 24 – a 41-9 drubbing at the hands of Baylor one week after the BYU victory, a last-second touchdown to beat Kansas, and a 13-point home loss to an Arizona State team that had to fly to Orlando the day of the game. Long story short, what UCF team are we going to see on Friday? We really don't know, and that's why I trust Iowa State in this spot. There's probably going to be a nice dose of cardinal and gold inside the Bounce House for this game, but that's not the only reason why I'm picking the Cyclones. The other reason why this game favors Iowa State is the weather. It's going to be a rainy slugfest in Orlando, but the Cyclones have the pleasure of having Aiden Flora on their team. He's doing incredible things every week and should get plenty of carries with a likely run-first game plan here. Neither defense is very good, but Flora is going to be the difference yet again. The Cyclones clinch bowl eligibility in the Sunshine State. Prediction: Iowa State 31, UCF 23

away.headline: Iowa State women's coach Bill Fennelly suspended for a game for `inappropriate contact' with player
away.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Fennelly will sit out at Northern Iowa on Wednesday night. Associate head coach Caroline McCombs will direct the team that night. AMES, Iowa (AP) — Iowa State suspended women’s basketball coach Bill Fennelly one game Sunday night for “inappropriate contact” with a Cyclones player. Fennelly nudged the player’s head with his hand earlier Sunday in a 69-64 home victory over Illinois Chicago. The 69-year-old Bill Fennelly said last month he plans to retire at the end of the season, his 32nd as head coach at the school. “We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not,” athletic director Jared Benko said in a statement. “We have high expectations of all of our coaches, staff and student-athletes and we will not shy away from holding accountable those who fail to meet those expectations. I have met with Coach Fennelly and he has apologized to the student-athlete involved and regrets his actions.” “I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone Nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game,” Fennelly said in a statement. “I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way. I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward.” The Cyclones are 5-0 this season. Fennelly is 661-335 with 24 NCAA Tournament appearances and 26 postseason appearances at Iowa State. away.blurb: UCF Senior Ruled Out For Senior Knight vs. Iowa State: Injury Report Breakdown Skip to main content SI.COM In addition to only one defensive back being ruled out in UCF's Tuesday player availability report, the Knights are trending toward getting back their leading rusher against the Cyclones. The Knights are trending toward relief in the secondary, with both DJ Bell and Kahmel Johnson ruled probable in Tuesday's report. However, the unit won't be fully all-hands-on-deck, as Demari Henderson was ruled out . As for Bell, a senior, and Johnson, they are set to return to their rotational roles, barring any setbacks. Bell, after missing four games, would be back rotating with Jayden Bellamy and Antione Jackson . Johnson, after missing two games, would return as the backup nickelback behind Braeden Marshall . Three Knights were ruled questionable in Tuesday's report. Another senior that is questionable for Friday's Senior Knight game is linebacker Jayden Jennings , who, despite being on the Knights' reports for eight weeks of conference games, has always managed to play. He has only been designated questionable for one of these weeks before this one, however. So, should he miss Friday's game, Tackett Curtis and Jahleel Culbreath would be in line to take on greater roles in the Knights' linebacker rotation. Finally, after missing last weekend's game against Arizona State, Waden Charles has the chance to return after just a one-game absence. Should he be out for a second game, however, the Knights would still have several receiving threats in the form of Josh Derry , Tyren Hornes , Duane Thomas Jr. and tight end Caden Piening . WEDNESDAY UPDATE: Charles was upgraded to probable for the Knights' Wednesday report. Joining Bell and Johnson in getting designated probable are Piening and running back Duke Watson . The designation implies a likely chance for Watson, the Knights' leading rusher this season, to return after missing Saturday's game against Arizona State. However, should he suffer any setbacks, he has Taevion Swint and Landen Chambers behind him. Meanwhile, Piening managed to play last Saturday against the Sun Devils, catching four passes for 35 yards, after going into the weekend with questionable designations. Carter made his return to the field on Saturday after a seven-game absence, making three tackles. Jenkins did not see the field on Saturday. However, given he was a game-time decision against the Sun Devils, he could very well be available against the Cyclones should Frost need him. away.blurb: That kind of leadership is going to pay dividends even if Toure isn’t on the court with his teammates currently. When he does return, the transition back to the hardwood is going to be a much smoother one given how involved he is currently. Having Lipsey back in the lineup for a fifth year has certainly been fortunate, helping compensate for Toure’s absence. When he does return, those two are going to combine to once again be the best defensive backcourt in the country. Killyan Toure Remaining Involved With Iowa State Despite Injury Skip to main content SI.COM The Iowa State Cyclones suffered a massive loss over the summer when it was revealed that guard Killyan Toure had to undergo a procedure for a shoulder injury . He will be sidelined for the entire non-conference schedule and will likely miss the start of the Big 12 as well. Expected to be a major part of the team’s game plan and viewed as an emerging star in men’s basketball, replacing Toure is no small task. He is an impactful player on both ends of the floor and improved as his freshman year went along. Head coach T.J. Otzelberger trusted him enough that he started every game of the 2025-26 season in the backcourt alongside Tamin Lipsey. While the talented guard hasn’t been able to get on the court yet this season, he is still making a positive impact on the team. Despite his youthfulness as a sophomore, he is showcasing some leadership skills and mentoring players who are newer to the program. home.headline: UCF LB Lewis Carter Reflects on Recovering From Injury
home.blurb: Kiffin's return to Tennessee Throughout the long seven weeks, including the bye, Carter said he kept his head down and attacked recovery. He made progress, and the Frost hinted at an inevitable return since Oct. 26. UCF's coach said the senior was a game-time decision before the Oct. 30 matchup against the Baylor Bears, and if not, he'd be a game-time decision on the road against the Kansas Jayhawks. Carter didn't return in either. However, Frost's optimism about his availability was a positive sign that the Knights' defense would get their captain back. UCF LB Lewis Carter Reflects on Recovering From Injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF 'GTA 6' impacts sports UCF LB Lewis Carter Reflects on Recovering From Injury (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) Demetrius Montero · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 18, 2026 at 12:36 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Lewis Carter missed six straight conference games before returning in the UCF Knights ' 26-13 loss to the Arizona State Sun Devils last Saturday. Carter sustained a knee injury in Week 3 against the Georgia State Panthers, as fans and media saw him enter the medical tent. Coach Scott Frost said he was unaware his senior was injured, and it spiraled into missing the star linebacker. Their captain made his conference debut against Arizona State. He had a quiet performance, posting three solo tackles. The star linebacker said he's 100% and wants to put his best foot forward to help his team win. UCF is one win away from a bowl game, snapping a two-year drought. Carter quarterbacks the defense, communicates adjustments when the offense audibles and shores up tackling. He led the team with 92 tackles last season and was on pace to continue wearing the crown until he got injured. UCF sorely missed his presence over the middle, but its depth stepped up. Tackett Curtis is the team's leading tackler with a career-high 67 tackles, two passes defended, two sacks and two interceptions. Jahleel Culbreath and Jayden Jennings have contributed alongside Curtis. They tallied 67 tackles, three pass deflections and 1.5 sacks. The Knights' front seven got its best linebacker back during a crucial Friday game against the Cyclones. Frost said they will be a " good challenge " with a dual-threat quarterback and the Big 12's leading rusher. Aiden Flora leads with 1,335 yards and is second with 12 touchdowns. Flora has tallied five 150-plus-yard games and four multi-touchdown games. He rushed for a career-high 221 yards in a 51-49 upset over the then-No. 24 Oklahoma State Cowboys and reached a career-best three touchdowns twice: once in a 45-42 win over the West Virginia Mountaineers and in a 41-13 blowout over the Cincinnati Bearcats. Carter's ability to blow up the run game is what UCF needs to avenge last week's disappointing loss and send him off with one final home win

UCF Running Back Ruled Out For Arizona State Game: Injury Report Breakdown
home.blurb: UCF Running Back Ruled Out For Arizona State Game: Injury Report Breakdown Skip to main content SI.COM The highest-profile name officially out for Saturday's game against the Sun Devils is running back Duke Watson , UCF's primary rusher so far this season. He had just two carries last Saturday in Lawrence before an injury took him out of the game. He was shown on ESPN2's broadcast later in the game in street clothes and wearing a walking boot. Watson's injury comes fresh off the return of fellow running back Taevion Swint , who was out for two games with an injury of his own. He now stands to gain some more touches due to Watson's absence alongside Landen Chambers , who had his own injury during the Kansas game, but his absence from the Knights' Wednesday report indicates he is a go for Saturday. While the Knights are going to be without one rusher against Arizona State, there is a chance they may also be without two pass catchers as well, as wide receiver Waden Charles has been designated doubtful and tight end Caden Piening has been designated questionable . FRIDAY UPDATE: Charles was offically ruled out for Saturday's game in the Knights' Friday report. Quarterback Keyone Jenkins was designated questionable on Wednesday, though with Alonza Barnett III back and healthy, his status is more of a question about who the Knights' backup quarterback is going to be. Should Jenkins need to sit another game, freshman Rocco Marriott , who saw the field briefly in Kansas, would likely take up the role. All three of the Knights' defensive backs that were sidelined last weekend against Kansas: Demari Henderson , DJ Bell and Kahmel Johnson are once again ruled out for Saturday's game against Arizona State. This is going to mark Henderson's third missed game of the season, the third for Bell and the second for Johnson. The sidelined trio were not the only defensive backs featured in UCF's report, as Antione Jackso n and Ty Bartrum were both designated probable on Wednesday. Bartrum was labeled probable last weekend as well and went on to play. So, barring any setbacks, both should see the field on Saturday. After missing the first six games of conference play, linebacker Lewis Carter is on the verge of returning to the field after receiving a probable designation. Coach Scott Frost said he had his fingers crossed for him during his Monday press conference. Carter's return would actually make UCF's linebacker room deeper. In the time he's been injured, Cole Kozlowski was given a temporary injunction that allowed him to play for the Knights this season. So, accounting for Carter's return, UCF could now feature a five-man rotation at linebacker with Carter, Kozlowski, Tackett Curtis , Jahleel Culbreath and Jayden Jennings , the latter of which was also designated probable for Saturday's game. That job gets tougher with Andrew Marshall out. Carriker talks through how Nebraska can mix up its pressure and make Ohio State work for its yards. Nebraska just shut out a Big Ten opponent on the road. The Huskers dispatched Rutgers 31–0 on Saturday, and while the Scarlet Knights aren't exactly setting the college football world on fire, shutting out a conference opponent is no small accomplishment. Now comes Ohio State. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Ohio State mascot Brutus joins the Ohio State Buckeyes in the singing of "Carmen Ohio" following a 28-19 victory over the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Normally, that name alone would be enough to make Nebraska fans start calculating how much bourbon they'll need by halftime. But these aren't the same Buckeyes we've grown accustomed to seeing. Ohio State has three losses. Three! In Columbus, that's practically grounds for declaring a state of emergency. And according to Ramsey from Eleven Warriors, who joined Monday Night Therapy this week, the problems aren't imaginary. The offensive line has struggled. The tight ends apparently believe blocking is an optional extracurricular activity. Special teams have been an adventure, and not the enjoyable kind. The Buckeyes are also starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who's talented but still learning on the job. Those are a lot of vulnerabilities for a program accustomed to simply reloading every season. Of course, Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs with the ball as Damon Walters #21 of the Northwestern Wildcats defends during the fourth quarter of a game at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images And therein lies the problem. Smith might be the best receiver in college football. Nebraska can scheme, disguise coverages, and pressure the quarterback all afternoon, but Smith is capable of making one play that changes everything. So how does Nebraska keep him from doing that? Run. The. Damn. Ball. Control possession. Move the chains. Keep the clock running. Make Ohio State's offense spend as much time watching from the sideline as possible. And when it's third-and-two, perhaps we could actually gain two yards instead of getting unnecessarily creative. Just a thought. Nebraska's defense has momentum after its performance against Rutgers, and a home crowd in Lincoln should make life uncomfortable for a freshman quarterback. The opportunity is there. But opportunity and execution haven't always been particularly close friends in Lincoln. Nebraska vs. Ohio State Betting Odds The betting discussion has centered on Ohio State as a narrow favorite. The FanDuel Sportsbook currently has the visitors as a 3.5-point favorite. The over/under is currently 41.5 points. Personally, I think Ohio State would deserve to be favored by six or seven points on a neutral field. But Memorial Stadium isn't neutral, and this isn't an Ohio State team without weaknesses. The Buckeyes have the talent to win this game. Nebraska has the opportunity to make that talent irrelevant for long stretches. Whether the Huskers can actually pull that off is another question entirely. Choose wisely. Play responsibly. And Go Big Red. Always.

Gratz) 1 / 2 Washington Nebraska Football Washington Nebraska Football Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nebraska's 31-game losing streak against teams in The Associated Press Top 25 is one of the great mysteries of college football. Yes, the Cornhuskers have been in a down cycle for two-plus decades. But it's hard to believe a program still among the winningest in history hasn't beaten a ranked opponent since a 35-32 win over Oregon on Sept. 17, 2016. Only Rutgers, at 46 in a row, has a longer losing streak against the Top 25. The Huskers' skid has covered the coaching runs of Mike Riley, Scott Frost, interim coach Mickey Joseph and now Matt Rhule, whose personal losing streak against the Top 25 stands at 21 over a combined seven seasons at Baylor and Nebraska. Nebraska nearly broke through against then-No. 7 Indiana on Oct. 10. The Huskers entered the fourth quarter leading by 11 points and lost 20-17. The next opportunity comes Saturday when No. 16 Ohio State visits. If the Huskers lose, they will presumably get another chance the day after Thanksgiving at Iowa, which is No. 13 this week. The picks, with AP rankings and betting lines, for FBS vs. FBS matchups. All games are on Saturday unless noted: No. 1 Georgia (minus 16 1/2) at South Carolina Bulldogs are rolling right now and the injuries are piling up for South Carolina, which was without QB LaNorris Sellers in last week's loss to Arkansas. Pick: Georgia 38-14. No. 2 Utah (minus 7) at TCU Aside from BYU, this will be the toughest defense the unbeaten Utes have faced. Horned Frogs' problem is offense, or lack of it. Pick: Utah 24-13. SMU (plus 20 1/2) at No. 3 Notre Dame Fighting Irish are on track for the playoff and aren't about to slow down. Mustangs won't win, but they won't let the game get away from them like they did in last week's 42-point home loss to Wake Forest. Pick: Notre Dame 33-20. No. 4 UCLA (minus 3 1/2) at Michigan Unbeaten Bruins have been better on road than at home. Wolverines have major injury issues, and their 24-point loss to Oregon was their most lopsided in six years. Pick: UCLA 27-21. Virginia Tech (plus 21) at No. 5 Miami Hokies have allowed 91 points while getting clobbered two weeks in a row, and another sound beating is in store if they don't shore things up. Pick: Miami 35-17. No. 6 Indiana (minus 8) at Washington Hoosiers' offense seems to be perking up with Grant Wilson at QB — hey, the CFP committee noticed! — and their defense is poised to build on its Big Ten-leading sack total against an offensive line that's battled injuries. Pick: Indiana 26-14. Arkansas at No. 8 Texas (minus 20 1/2) Longhorns won't let last week's comeback win at LSU go to waste against an Arkansas team that's lost 14 straight road games against ranked SEC opponents. Pick: Texas 34-10. LSU (minus 1) at No. 9 Tennessee It's all about the run game for Tennessee, and Tigers have held three straight and seven of 10 opponents under 100 yards on the ground. Pick: LSU 24-21. No. 10 Wake Forest (minus 20 1/2) at Georgia Tech Demon Deacons' 44-points-per-game offense goes against a Georgia Tech defense allowing 43 per game against ACC opponents excluding last week's 20-6 win at Clemson. Pick: Wake Forest 45-20. No. 11 Texas Tech (minus 3 1/2) at Baylor Tech QB Thomas Castellanos has averaged 342 yards per game in total offense and thrown for 11 TDs with no interceptions in three starts since replacing Will Hammond. Pick: Texas Tech 33-27. No. 12 BYU at Kansas (plus 5 1/2) Cougars' playoff hopes depend on their defense's ability to keep dual-threat QB Isaiah Marshall under control. Pick: BYU 27-24. No. 13 Iowa (minus 8) at Illinois Carson Boyd, with 22 career snaps, could make his first start for Illinois against a top-10 Iowa defense that leads nation in red zone defense. Pick: Iowa 31-17. No. 14 Oregon (minus 16) at Michigan State Ducks comes into the Friday night game leading Big Ten in pass plays of 20-plus yards, and Spartans are prone to giving up big chunks through the air. Pick: Oregon 36-19. San Diego State at No. 15 Boise State (minus 16 1/2) Broncos QB Maddux Madsen had a career game against Oregon State in his first game back from injury. Aztecs are giving up more than 500 yards and 47 points per game on the road. Pick: Boise State 52-28. No. 16 Ohio State at Nebraska (plus 3) The time has come for Cornhuskers to end their 31-game losing streak against AP Top 25 opponents. Their defense will make it happen. Pick: Nebraska 24-21. No. 17 Kentucky (plus 5 1/2) at Missouri Both have lost two in a row and faded from the playoff picture. Kentucky allowed total of 451 rushing yards to Tennessee and Florida. Run game has been Mizzou's strength, but not as much lately. Pick: Missouri 27-26. Maryland at No. 18 Southern California (minus 17 1/2) Terrapins have won two straight under interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim. They haven't won three in a row in conference play since 2006. Pick: USC 41-21. No. 19 Arizona (minus 7) at Kansas State Arizona lost a heartbreaker to Utah at home and will go on the road to take out some frustration against an opponent that's lost four straight and six of seven. Pick: Arizona 35-14. No. 20 Houston at West Virginia (plus 8 1/2) Houston gave up a season-high 249 rushing yards to Colorado. Mountaineers tandem of Cam Cook and Michael Hawkins, averaging a combined 203 yards per game on the ground, were shut down by Kansas. Pick: Houston 44-41. Pittsburgh (plus 14) at No. 21 Louisville Cardinals need to ratchet up their offense. They will play first half without leading tackler Stanquan Clark, who was suspended for his role in postgame fracas with North Carolina. Pick: Louisville 26-17. Western Kentucky at No. 22 Liberty (minus 17) Liberty should be able to unleash its Conference USA-best run game against a defense giving up more than 5 yards per rushing attempt. Pick: Liberty 42-21. Vanderbilt at No. 23 Florida (minus 13 1/2) Everything is contingent on which version of the Gators show up — the one that's beaten three ranked opponents or the one soundly beaten at home by South Carolina and Oklahoma. Pick: Florida 29-14. No. 24 Memphis (minus 3 1/2) at Navy Marcus Stokes, who has four straight 300-yard passing games, will be the difference in a game featuring top-10 rushing offenses. Pick: Memphis 35-28. AP predictions scorecard Last week: Straight-up — 14-7; Against spread — 11-10. Season: Straight-up — 138-56; Against spread — 96-96-2. home.headline: Nebraska’s OSU injury report is rough, but Anthony Jones' return could be bright spot
home.blurb: Defensive back Andrew Marshall is out , as Matt Rhule announced earlier this week that one of the nation's top cornerbacks will miss the rest of Nebraska’s season. The good news for the Huskers is that defensive lineman Anthony Jones Jr. was upgraded from “out” last week to “questionable” this week. With this being the first injury report of the week, there’s now hope that he could be upgraded to probable by Friday and then suit up on Saturday morning. For Ohio State, the guys who are out were all expected to be out. Quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Ja'Kobi Jackson, safety Deshawn Stewart, wide receiver Brennen Schramm, offensive linemen Jaxon Powell and Max Riley, and tight end Maxence LeBlanc will miss the game against the Cornhuskers. Nebraska football loses Owen Chambliss, Jahsear Whittington but Anthony Jones could return The Ohio State players who are questionable are safety Terry Moore, wide receiver Brock Boyd, safety Brenten "Inky" Jones, linebacker Eli Lee, and offensive lineman Phillip Daniels. The biggest piece of positive news for the Buckeyes is that senior left guard Luke Montgomery is expected to return. Montgomery is ready to roll after not appearing on the report, while both Daniels and Boyd are listed as questionable. Montgomery and Daniels had flu-like symptoms last week, while Boyd has been battling a sprained ankle for more than a month. No surprises popped up on the availability report for Ohio State, unlike last week when Montgomery was initially listed as questionable. That suggests the Buckeyes avoided any major new injuries in their win over Northwestern. Of course, the biggest absence of all for OSU is quarterback Julian Sayin. That might not be as big a problem for Ryan Day and company after his replacement, Luke Fahey , finally had a very solid outing. Against Northwestern, Fahey completed 21 of 32 passes for 201 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also threw an interception, but the biggest step forward was that he seemed to figure out a secret to the offense: Just get the ball to Jeremiah Smith. Without Owen Chambliss, Jahsear Whittington, and Andrew Marshall, Nebraska will have its work cut out for it on Saturday morning. home.headline: Andrew Marshall injury could keep Nebraska from taking the next step in evolution
home.blurb: Marshall missed the Huskers’ game against Rutgers this past weekend, and on Monday, head coach Matt Rhule confirmed that the star defensive back is out for the rest of the season. When Nebraska faces off against Ohio State on Saturday, the Huskers know they won’t have to face quarterback Julian Sayin . However, they’ll still have to face all-time great wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, which is why losing Andrew Marshall is a big blow. Rhule said that Marshall suffered a stress fracture in his leg against Illinois but continued to play after suffering the injury. Since that game, Marshall has undergone surgery to repair the fracture and has played his last down for Nebraska in his college football career. Marshall finished the 2026 season with 28 tackles, an interception, and a team-high six pass breakups. He’s long been considered one of the best defensive backs in the country, and Rhule made that point when addressing the injury. Andrew Marshall season-ending injury leaves Nebraska football without shutdown corner vs. Ohio State “I think he’s as good as there is in the country and I think everyone knows it,” Rhule said during his Monday press conference. “I think everyone’s seen it.” The California native is one of NU’s best transfer-portal stories after arriving from Idaho before the 2025 campaign. Nebraska routinely lined him up opposite an opponent’s best receiver and often left him in one-on-one coverage while devoting defensive help elsewhere. Marshall was targeted just 44 times this season and allowed just 15 receptions for 237 yards. 93 of those yards came against Illinois, as it was easily his worst game of the season. Playing on a bum leg certainly explains why he struggled against Illinois’ Colin Dixon, who was recently named to the latest Fred Biletnikoff Award watch list. Nebraska started Victor Evans and freshman Danny Odem at cornerback against Rutgers and will move forward with the same duo along with Jeremiah Charles. Junior Larry Tarver is also set to see more rotational action. Without Nebraska’s shutdown corner, beating Ohio State became even tougher on Monday. It’s unlikely that one corner will be assigned to Smith the way defensive coordinator Rob Aurich might have assigned Marshall if he were healthy. Nebraska is obviously hoping that a change in offensive coordinator and the end of the four-game losing streak will allow the Huskers to finish the season strong. Beating Ohio State in Lincoln is never easy, but this version of the Buckeyes has shown they are flawed. A loss on Saturday will almost certainly be taken as a sign Dana Holgorsen firing shows Nebraska has officially entered panic mode Nebraska's offense doesn’t need reinvention it needs Glenn Thomas to see the obvious Tristan Alvano’s resurgence exposes Nebraska’s brutal kicking regression KJ Duff injury leaves Nebraska even fewer excuses against struggling Rutgers Addison Williams says Nebraska’s pressure-moment failures come down to habits This article was originally

picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL As the Badgers' seesaw of a 2026 season rolls on, Wisconsin once finds itself on the wrong end of a tough loss after collapsing on the road against Maryland . Sitting at 6-4 (4-3 in the B1G), head coach Luke Fickell and company are running out of time to prove that they're guiding this program in the right direction. A resounding win over an inferior opponent , bouncing back from a mind-numbing loss in the process, would be a great start. I've got three bold predictions for the Badgers' clash with the Boilermakers in West Lafayette. Colton Joseph recaptures the hearts of Badgers fans Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. If Joseph indeed gets the starting nod in place of an injured Hopkins, it's not hard to see him playing well and in the process, winning back the hearts of some Badgers fans despite his well-documented struggles this season. First of all, Joseph should have no shortage of motivation. He was benched for a true freshman, and now gets his shot to prove that was a big mistake. That's a situation any competitor dreams of, and say what you will about Joseph; he's certainly a competitor. What's more, after getting benched for Hopkins and with the future of the entire coaching staff potentially up in the air this offseason, Joseph needs to put good things on tape should he be forced to enter the transfer portal again this winter. At best, he's proved dynamic yet inconsistent at the Big Ten level and at worst, he's been a turnover machine with limited arm talent. If Hopkins is forced to sit out one or both of the final two games this fall, these contests are massively important for Joseph's future; how he plays could determine whether he remains at the Power Four level in 2027. Finally, Purdue's defense is extremely permeable . It has the worst total defense in the Big Ten (417.3 yards per game) and the second-worst passing defense in the conference (239.0 yards per game). Purdue struggles to get consistent pressure (13 sacks across 10 games) and doesn't force turnovers with regularity. If there's any defense for Joseph to carve through, it's the Boilermakers. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Purdue's Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten and 20th nationally with 2,418 passing yards. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Still, dive into Browne's performance this season, and the numbers are a tad misleading. The quarterback hasn't eclipsed 300 passing yards since Week 3 against UCLA, and while that's certainly an impressive feat given how strong the Bruins' defense is, he's struggled pretty mightily against the other top defenses he's faced. In fact, Browne has been held under 160 passing yards in four of his last seven outings. Against the top passing defenses he's played such as Penn State (No. 3 nationally in passing yards allowed per game) as well as Iowa and Minnesota (both of whom rank inside the top-45 in passing yards allowed), he's had a rough go of it. The Nittany Lions held him to 142 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions on 34 percent completion. Iowa limited him to 158 yards, one touchdown and one interceptions. And while Purdue blew out Minnesota, Brown only collected 159 passing yards, one score and 58 percent completion. Wisconsin's pass defense, meanwhile, checks in at No. 25 in the country. And while it just allowed Maryland's backup to complete 21-of-23 passes last week, the Badgers' defense has managed to bounce back from its poor performances this season. It'll need to run it back in West Lafayette. The Badgers' offensive line looks passable This might be the boldest prediction of the three, considering how much of a struggle its been up front for Wisconsin. Last week against Maryland, the Badgers' offensive line struggled mightily in pass protection, allowing four sacks. It wasn't much better in the run game, as Wisconsin backs created just 3.3 yards per carry and also suffered six tackles-for-loss. Still, Maryland's lowly record did well to disguise just how capable its front seven actually is. For how bad the Terps have been this fall, their defensive front is pretty loaded with capable playmakers. The same can't be said for Purdue. The Boilermakers have just 13 sacks on the season, firmly placing them into the bottom tier of teams; only 14 FBS programs have fewer. They've created 107 total pressures, which is harder to contextualize nationally but compared with Wisconsin's 145 total pressures, they're a clear step down. Their run defense, meanwhile, surrenders 178.3 yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Their defense as a whole has collected 205 stops, or tackles that constitute a failure for the offense, compared to Wisconsin's 276. Translation? They don't penetrate the backfield or win at the point of attack nearly as well as the Badgers. Despite what could be a patchwork offensive line this week, I still expect Wisconsin to find success up front. The latest odds for Wisconsin vs. Purdue paint a sad reality for Luke Fickell
picks.blurb: The latest odds for Wisconsin vs. Purdue paint a sad reality for Luke Fickell Skip to main content About Us Wisconsin Badgers News Wisconsin Football Wisconsin Basketball FanSided NCAA Sites Wisconsin Badgers In The Pros Wisconsin Football Recruiting Wisconsin Football All-Time Lists Wisconsin Basketball Recruiting Wisconsin Women's Basketball Wisconsin Basketball All-Time Lists The Wisconsin Badgers were terrible against the Maryland Terrapins on Saturday. There's no other way to slice it or dice it, it was disgraceful at best and a 'fire everybody in the whole football department' at worst. Which is what many of the Wisconsin fans are calling for. Maryland had only one Big Ten game all season and had fired their head coach. The Terrapins are a basement-dwelling Big Ten team. So, what does Vegas do for Wisconsin when the Badgers take on another basement-dwelling team, Purdue? Well, they give them barely favorable odds. Can't trust them. The best thing Wisconsin has going for itself in this Purdue game is that it's the Boilermakers that the Terrapins beat a couple of games ago. The Badgers enter their final road game of the season against a *checks notes* 3-7 Purdue team as barely a favorite. At 5.5 points, Vegas assumes that Wisconsin can only beat the Boilermakers with two field goals... or worse. That's alarming and paints a bleak reality for Luke Fickell. In his banner year, the "prove-it" year, the one when everything lined up perfectly. He had the bigger budget, the supposedly better coaching staff, a deeper quarterback room, a way more favorable schedule, and yet, with only two games to go, Wisconsin is barely considered a favorite over Purdue. It's hard to express how disappointing that is, when Wisconsin should be looking at this game as a "rest the starters" in the 4th-quarter situation; they are staring down the barrel of another potential upset. If there's anything that shows Wisconsin should move on from Luke Fickell and/or some of his staff, it's this bleak reminder that the program is actually in the same place as last year, but with an easier schedule. ESPN has the probabilities a bit higher than Vegas at 65% according to their analytics, but still, that's not great. And if Wisconsin can't find a way to beat Purdue, and beat them without any drama, there's no reason Luke Fickell needs to get on the flight back to Madison. And yet the big fear is that this 6-win season will be sold to Wisconsin fans as a step forward and that the Badgers should continue to let him run it back. The $21 million buy-out may force Shawn Eichorst to gaslight the fanbase, as Chris McIntosh did. Hopefully, I'm wrong, but it feels like we are headed that direction. This Purdue game needs to be a blowout; winning by 5 or 6 points won't be good enough. Fans should be embarrassed that Vegas even suggests so. Hopkins certainly deserves criticism for his performance, but offensive coordinator Jeff Grimes' questionable play-calling and an inconsistent rushing attack did little to put him in an ideal position to succeed. Darrion Dupree handled the bulk of the workload, rushing 14 times for 57 yards (4.1 YPC) and two scores while adding four receptions for 21 yards. The junior was responsible for both Wisconsin touchdowns, scoring from four yards out in the first quarter and punching in a one-yard run early in the fourth. However, his third-quarter fumble proved devastating, handing Maryland possession deep in Wisconsin territory and setting up a touchdown that gave the Terrapins their first lead. The offensive line's continued inability to establish consistent running lanes complicates the evaluation, and Dupree had his share of positive moments. Nevertheless, his costly turnover and the group's limited overall production prevent a higher grade. That general sentiment can be applied to the receiving corps as a whole, which has struggled to establish any consistency amid the offense's recurring dysfunction. away.headline: Wisconsin football gets bad news on Javan Robinson, O-line from initial Purdue injury report
away.blurb: With two games to play in the regular season, however, that luck may be running out . Wisconsin's initial injury report lists starting cornerback and the Badgers' best cover man in the secondary, Javan Robinson, as doubtful for Saturday afternoon. That means barring a significant development, Wisconsin will be without its top cornerback and another veteran leader in the secondary. Starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins, who Fickell sounded encouraged about on Monday, is listed as questionable. Right now, it looks like a toss-up if he'll be able to play despite Fickell saying earlier in the week that "Hopefully he'll be fine...luckily it's not his throwing side." Wisconsin's starting right tackle Emerson Mandell is also listed as questionable. He wasn't noticeably banged up last week against the Terps, so Fickell wasn't asked about his status on Monday. However, he's now a question mark as well, and with Barrett Nelson also unavailable for the past three weeks, Wisconsin could be forced to start a tackle tandem of PJ Wilkins and Lucas Simmons-Johansson. That's certainly less than ideal, although the latter did just play a career-high 26 snaps against Maryland. Though Robinson almost certainly being out and the uncertainty around Hopkins and Mandell is disheartening, the Badgers did receive some good news on the injury front. Their other starting cornerback Jai'mier Scott, who didn't play last week in College Park, is listed as probable, as is star pass-rusher Sebastian Cheeks. Getting those two back would do wonders to mitigate the damage this defense has already suffered. Regardless of how the week shakes out, Wisconsin is going to have to take down Purdue somewhat short-handed. Wisconsin Football is Running Out of Time to Fix its Ground Game Other than the constant shuffling on the offensive line, much of which was caused at least initially by injuries suffered before the season began, Wisconsin football has had a relatively clean bill of health for much of the year, especially considering head coach Luke Fickell's past injury luck in Madison. When Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3 B1G) travels to face Purdue (3-7, 2-5 B1G) on Saturday afternoon in West Lafayette, it could be without several key starters in a game that's critically important for Fickell and company to bounce back and win after the late collapse in College Park last weekend. We already knew that starting safety Matt Jung was lost for the season, joining the likes of offensive tackle Kevin Heywood and cornerback Cai Bates. But the Badgers' initial injury report poses more questions than answers ahead of a game against Purdue in which, again, Wisconsin could really use a bounce-back victory on the road. Belichick said earlier in the week that Edwards was “getting better.” Edwards, in his sixth season in college football, has completed 65.5% of his passes. He has 18 touchdowns and six interceptions. North Carolina defensive back Greg Smith III was suspended by the ACC for the first half of the Virginia game for his actions in a postgame fight with Louisville. He is listed as out for Saturday’s game. Smith leads the Tar Heels with three interceptions and has a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He has 56 tackles, including three for loss, in 10 games. Defensive end Melkart Abou Jaoude, who missed time earlier in the season with a broken bone in his right hand, is also out for Saturday’s game. Abou Jaoude has 21 tackles, including two sacks, in addition to a team-high nine quarterback hurries in eight games this season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings The unbeaten Bruins can clinch a Big Ten title game berth, but the struggling Wolverines have a clear path to shock their new conference rival if they protect the football Getty Images Michigan has fallen so far under Kyle Whittingham that the all-time winningest program in college football has been reduced to being a home underdog against a UCLA program that won three games last season. The No. 4 Bruins are arriving for their first game at Michigan Stadium since 1996 on Saturday in prime position to reach the Big Ten Championship Game and College Football Playoff. The Wolverines team hosting them is scraping rock bottom after falling to 5-5 with a 31-7 loss at Oregon last week. It's a jarring backdrop for the first battle between these teams as Big Ten foes. At 10-0 (7-0 Big Ten), the Bruins are one win away from reaching 11 victories for the first time in program history. Just three years removed from a national championship, Michigan may be on the cusp of yet another coaching change. Lauded as a stabilizing hire amid a tumultuous ending to Sherrone Moore's tenure last year, Whittingham has presided over a disaster. Michigan ranks 131st of 138 FBS teams in total offense, averaging just 300.9 yards per game. While the Wolverines have quickly reached dire straits under Whittingham, 66, they can play the role of spoiler over the season's final two weeks. Handing UCLA its first loss and/or upsetting rival Ohio State to close the season would bring some morsel of satisfaction to what has been a painful 2026 slog in Ann Arbor. Michigan vs. UCLA: Need to know What's at stake for UCLA: Despite its 10-0 record, UCLA is still not a lock for the College Football Playoff. The Bruins' relative lack of marquee victories means they need to win at least one of their final two regular-season games to have a solid at-large case. The CBS Sports CFP Forecaster gives UCLA an 86.1% chance of making the field with a win over the Wolverines. A win would also lock up a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game for the Bruins, who close the regular season against crosstown rival USC next week. Can Wayne Knight break free?: Wayne Knight rattled off three straight 100-plus yard rushing performances during UCLA's first three Big Ten victories. But in the past five games, the James Madison transfer has eclipsed the century mark just once. Last week's 22-14 win over Illinois marked his first game this season without either a rushing or receiving touchdown. After averaging 253.2 rushing yards per game on 6.1 yards per attempt in their first five games, the Bruins have averaged just 152.2 yards per game on 4.1 yards per attempt over their last five. If there's one thing Michigan does reasonably well, it's defend the run. Opponents are averaging just 103.1 yards per game on the ground against the Wolverines. Ongoing quarterback battle: With two games left in the regular season, there still isn't an established starting quarterback at Michigan. It's been that kind of season for the Wolverines, who played both Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr in last week's loss to Oregon. Interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding boiled this week's competition between the two signal-callers down to ball security. "Are you going to necessarily have an epiphany that in Week 11 the kid can do this particular thing?" Harding said. "I would not say that that's the case, but I think what you can evaluate in practice this week is who's valuing the importance of having the football at the end of the play. That honestly is the main piece in the evaluation is who can take care of the football." The Wolverines have edged quality foes Oklahoma and Penn State by winning the turnover battle, and they took Indiana to overtime while winning it 2-1. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Scotty White · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan football season felt over when the Wolverines lost to Michigan State, and that defeat seems to have had a similar impact on the team. Michigan lost on the road against Oregon, 31-7, last weekend, and it didn't look like anyone was mentally present for the Wolverines. This weekend presents a new challenge — the UCLA Bruins. UCLA is having a special season, especially considering this was one of the worst teams in the Big Ten last year. The Bruins are 10-0 and knocking on the doorstep of the Big Ten Championship and College Football Playoff. A win this weekend would clinch the Bruins a spot in Indy, and it would likely make it impossible for them to miss the CFP. Somehow, UCLA is only favored by 3.5 points leading up to this game. Does Vegas know something, or will it be another uninspiring performance from the Wolverines? Let's make some bold predictions for the game. Michigan will go to another backup QB The Oregon game was interesting, as Michigan went back-and-forth between Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood, waiting for someone to provide a spark. The thing is, I really don't think it matters. I don't think the issue is with the quarterbacks at all, as I think Underwood and Carr have both shown some good flashes. I believe the real issue boils down to poor offensive line play and the refusal to involve the tight ends more. Still, the coaches are going to search for a spark. Brayden Fowler-Nicolosi, a transfer from Colorado State, should be next in line at the quarterback position. I'm honestly surprised we haven't seen him yet, but there's truly nothing to lose at this point. Give him a shot. Michigan gets shutout I don't like to reuse predictions in these, but I'm honestly shocked this hasn't happened yet and I feel like it's inevitable at this point. This offense has amazed us with levels of bad we didn't know existed, and I think it still has one more trick up its sleeve. UCLA is 10-0 in large part due to its defense. Remember, the Bruins have been without starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava since Oct. 10 when he got hurt at Oregon. Since then, only one team has hit 20 points against the Bruins. They are ranked No. 4 in the country in total defense. UCLA is shutting everyone down. Michigan barely avoided a shutout against Michigan State, a bad team with a bad defense. The Wolverines haven't been shutout at home since 1967, but that could change this weekend. UCLA wins, 17-0 UCLA is great defensively, but the Bruins have only eclipsed 30 points once with Ty Dieffenbach at quarterback, so I expect Michigan's defense to keep this one relatively close. Still, I just can't imagine the Wolverines finding any success offensively, and I would be shocked if UCLA doesn't easily cover the spread. Michigan's bowl hopes will hinge on The Game.

away.headline: UCLA endures injury scare, gets heroic return to stay unbeaten
away.blurb: It was a heroic return for the veteran who had departed UCLA’s game against Illinois just before halftime with a sore elbow and ankle. The crowd serenaded Dieffenbach with cheers anew once he came onto the field with his team holding a suddenly precarious lead over Illinois. All Dieffenbach did upon his return was to complete each of his five passes on the next drive, including a beautiful touchdown toss, to help the fourth-ranked Bruins hold on for a 22-14 victory that kept their unbeaten record intact. “That’s leadership, that stands out,” Chesney said, “and there’s the confidence everybody gained from that.” Illinois closed to within 19-14 after quarterback Katin Houser converted a huge fourth-down play, finding wide receiver Collin Dixon in the back of the end zone for a 7-yard touchdown with 7:14 left. But the Fighting Illini could conjure no more late magic after Houser went out with his own injury. “When we walked out there, I was like, damn, yes,” Chesney said of the crowd. “I knew we were on the brink of it and you were worried about the weather, but ultimately what a great job by them and really proud of the way they showed up.” After taking a shot in the arm, Ty Dieffenbach delivered one. Roars accompanied the previously injured UCLA quarterback with each step he took as he jogged back from the locker room to the Rose Bowl sideline late in the third quarter Friday night. “That crowd reaction was unbelievable,” Dieffenbach would say later. “I mean, that was one of the best moments of my life.” “They just don’t give up, they just don’t,” UCLA coach Bob Chesney said of his players. “They just believe they have a shot to win every game and they’re going to find a way.” The Bruins could exhale only after an Illinois pass fell incomplete over the middle with 43 seconds left. UCLA had registered another big defensive play only minutes earlier when safety Scooter Jackson came up with an interception – his second of the game – and returned it 41 yards to the Illinois 19-yard line with 2 minutes 42 seconds left. A short Mateen Bhaghani field goal gave the Bruins a 22-14 lead, necessitating a desperation drive by the Fighting Illini that came up well short. There were feel-good vibes all around after Dieffenbach escaped injury and UCLA improved to 10-0 for the first time since 1998 – the last season it won a conference championship. “No one believed that UCLA would be 10-0 this year, no one in the country, no one anywhere,” linebacker Sammy Omosigho said, “and we had to make them believe.” The Bruins, who are 7-0 in Big Ten games, need only one more victory in their final two regular-season games – against Michigan and USC – to clinch an appearance in the conference title game. Among other things, a season-high crowd of 45,800 celebrated a UCLA defense that intercepted three passes and registered five tackles for loss while holding the Fighting Illini (6-4, 4-3) to 240 yards of offense. away.headline: Ty Dieffenbach injury updates: UCLA QB returns after exiting in first half after hard hit
away.blurb: Kiffin's return to Tennessee He did not come out with the rest of the team out of halftime and did not return to the game to start the third quarter. UCLA's backup quarterback is Madden Iamaleava, the younger brother of Nico Iamaleava. He's in his second season with the Bruins and has seen limited action in his college career. Ty Dieffenbach injury updates: UCLA QB returns after exiting in first half after hard hit - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF 'GTA 6' impacts sports Jordan Mendoza, USA TODAY · USA TODAY Sports Sat, November 14, 2026 at 3:53 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads PASADENA, CA — UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach suffered an injury on a hard hit late in the first half against Illinois on Friday, Nov. 13. But it appears to not be an absolutely devastating hit for the Bruins . With 35 seconds left in the second quarter, Dieffenbach tried to throw the ball away when he got tripped up and was clearly in immediate pain. He was visibly shaken as he was attended to by support staff, and he appeared to indicate he had a left shoulder injury. After a few minutes he was helped up and taken to the sideline. Once the teams headed to the locker room, Dieffenbach went in appearing to not move his left arm and was limping. Ty Dieffenbach latest injury news Dieffenbach suffered an "upper body injury," according to the Fox broadcast. However, he emerged from the locker room with about four minutes left in the third quarter with a sleeve on his left arm, as the Rose Bowl crowd cheered. Dieffenbach was back on the field for UCLA late in the third quarter and played the remainder of the game. "I kind of went down a little awkward on the tackle, and my arm got caught up underneath, but it just got a little tight on me, and it's nothing serious," he said postgame. The Bruins got their quarterback to engineer another win. He reignited the offense, throwing a key fourth quarter touchdown to Semaj Morgan that strengthened the lead. UCLA held on to beat Illinois 22-14 to move to 10-0. Dieffenbach went 13-for-20 for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, with 28 rushing yards. The injury was a big scare to UCLA's quarterback room as Dieffenbach has played in place of starter Nico Iamaleava after Iamaleava suffered a season ending injury against Oregon on Oct. 10. Dieffenbach has stepped up and kept the Bruins one of two undefeated teams left in the country, at 9-0 for the first time since 1998 with a shot at their first College Football Playoff appearance. Prior to the injury, Dieffenbach was 8-for-13 for 168 yards with one touchdown and one interception, leading UCLA to a 10-0 lead over Illinois. home.headline: 2 Michigan football starters ruled out for UCLA game
home.blurb: Michigan football has ruled out two key starters for the game against UCLA – and could be down more than that. Wide receiver JJ Buchanan is lost for the season while offensive tackle Blake Frazier, who coach Kyle Whittingham said earlier in the week was a long shot to play, has also been ruled out, according to the Big Ten's availability report released on Wednesday, Nov. 18. But beyond that, five other starters are listed as questionable: wide receiver Andrew Marsh, edge rusher John Henry Daley, offensive lineman Brady Norton, safety Rod Moore and tight end Jalen Hoffman. With Buchanan out, Marsh is unquestionably the No. 1 pass-catching option. Marsh has a team-high 48 grabs that have led to 459 yards and one touchdown this season. Last week, he was targeted on 14 of Michigan's 20 passes between quarterbacks Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood. Moore tore his ACL in the spring of 2024 and missed all of that season. He tried to return in 2025 after more offseason complications with his knee, but suited up for just three games in the middle of the season before he was shut down the rest of the year. Channing Goodwin, Kendrick Bell and Jaylen Pile are all also listed as questionable. Hoffman has been one of U-M's most utilized tight ends this season, averaging 37 snaps per game the past four weeks and is second in the room with nine receptions for 78 yards. As for Moore, this will be the final game at Michigan Stadium for the sixth-year senior, who has won a national championship with the program and been an All-Big Ten player, but dealt with injury trouble the past two seasons. He's only missed one game this season at Rutgers, but played just six snaps the week prior against Indiana after appearing to injure his ankle on an interception against Penn State. Moore has 33 tackles, one interception and one pass defended this year. Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. home.blurb: We knew that JJ Buchanan was going to be out. Kyle Whittingham said so on Monday, but it's very concerning to see the likes of Andrew Marsh, and even Channing Goodwin to a certain extent on the list. Without Buchanan, Marsh is the certified alpha on the team and will be a key part of the Wolverines' passing attack — especially if there is any hope to get it going. And the offensive line remains a major issue. Blake Frazier is now officially out and the Wolverines played without him last weekend. Brady Norton is questionable, too, and the Wolverines could opt to play both Manuel Beigel and Marky Walbridge once again this weekend. After back-to-back losses to Michigan State and Oregon, the Wolverines are looking to get back in the win column. In fact, Michigan needs one more win in the last two weeks in order to go bowling. The Wolverines haven't missed a bowl game since 2014, the final year of Brady Hoke in Ann Arbor. If Michigan is going to gain bowl eligibility this weekend, the Wolverines are going to have to earn it. Michigan will host UCLA, which hasn't lost a game all year. The Bruins are one of the most surprising teams in college football. Despite losing Nico Iamaleava for the season, Bob Chesney has turned to his backup quarterback, but it's only resulted in success. If the Wolverines are going to beat UCLA , it's going to have to get the job done without a few players. Here's how Michigan's initial availability report looks heading into the Wolverines' Week 12 game against UCLA. More concern regarding the offense Michigan will also rely on Travis Johnson and Salesi Moa moving forward. Whittingham noted that tight end Mason Bonner could also see some play. It's also concerning to see Rod Moore on the list after he played last weekend against Oregon. The Wolverines' secondary got beat a few times against Oregon, and having a veteran back there like Moore would only help against UCLA. The Tigers moved to 6-4 in Lane Kiffin's first season after losing a heartbreaker against Texas 22-21 last week. Tennessee has been steady since making a quarterback change to George MacIntyre , winning five of its last six games. The Volunteers pulled away from Texas A&M in a 22-7 victory, led by a dominant defensive performance in College Station. LSU and Tennessee have not played since 2022, a 40-13 dominant for the Volunteers in Baton Rouge. Before that, the Tigers won five straight dating back to 2006. The Tigers sit at a paltry 6-4, including 0-4 against CFP-ranked opponents. LSU could desperately use even a single meaningful victory to build some momentum heading into 2027. Passing game woes: Tennessee started the year with freshman Faizon Brandon before handing the keys to George MacIntyre, but neither has provided much dynamism.
