Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Brett Davis-Imagn Images Zach Ragan · AtoZ Sports Wed, November 18, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Volunteers will host the LSU Tigers in Neyland Stadium on Saturday afternoon. Tennessee's College Football Playoff hopes are on the line this weekend against LSU. If the Vols beat LSU on Saturday in Neyland Stadium, they'll just need a win in the regular-season finale against Vanderbilt to lock down a spot in the College Football Playoff. But if Tennessee loses to LSU, they can likely kiss their playoff hopes goodbye. LSU, which has four losses, is out of the playoff picture. The Tigers' 6-4 record, however, isn't indicative of how good of a team they are. LSU has arguably the most talented roster in the nation, and they are just a couple of plays away from being 8-2. Tennessee has a 59% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 4% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). Combine that with the fact that Tennessee will be without several key players against the Tigers — specifically left guard Nic Moore and wide receiver Mike Matthews — and it's easy to see why there's some concern about this game on Rocky Top. Former Georgia QB Aaron Murray makes his prediction for LSU vs Tennessee Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray predicted last week that Tennessee would beat Texas A&M by 13 points last week (the Vols won by 15 points), but he's not making the same kind of prediction for the LSU game. Murray has the Tigers taking down the Vols on Saturday, predicting that LSU will leave Neyland Stadium with a 23-17 win. One of the main reasons Murray is predicting an LSU win is because the Vols will be without Mike Matthews. "This (LSU) defense is going to be able to put you in third-and-long situations," said Murray. "And they're going to be able to get to the quarterback with Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross coming off the edge. "… Can Tennessee's offense, without Matthews and with a banged up quarterback — it's possibly Faizon Brandon back in there playing quarterback — get the job done against LSU in this matchup? I don't feel very confident. Which is why I'm going with LSU 23-17 in this football game. If Mike Matthews was healthy, and if [George MacIntyre] — I don't know what the knee is right now, maybe he's 100 percent for the game [and I would feel different]. But still, no Mike Matthews. I think that's a big problem for the Tennessee Volunteers. So I think LSU wins the game." I think that's a fair prediction from Murray. There are certainly questions about the Vols' offense without Matthews. The junior wide receiver was easily Tennessee's most dynamic playmaker. But LSU has failed to finish games in the fourth quarter this season and that's an area where Tennessee has thrived. If the Vols can get this game to the fourth quarter, I like their chances. But if they get to the fourth quarter and they're down multiple scores, it could be too big of a hill for Tennessee's offense to climb. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:59 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Any thought that LSU was going to take the college football world by storm after Lane Kiffin took over ended with a tough 22-21 loss against Texas. It was the Tigers' fourth loss of the season, they're out of the College Football Playoff mix, and now it's time to play the spoiler role. Kiffin gets to play the villain, going back to his old coaching grounds – he was the Tennessee head coach in 2009 – and Tennessee will be fired up. The Vols are 8-2 after winning five of their last six games, and at No. 9 in the latest rankings, they're all but in the CFP if they win their last two games. LSU vs Tennessee: Quick Hits LSU closes out on the road at Arkansas after this. Lose to the Vols, and it'll be the third year in a row the program suffered a three-game losing streak. Tennessee goes to Vanderbilt to finish up the regular season. If it wins the final two games, it's in the mix for the SEC Championship along with the CFP. The two programs haven't met since 2022 – a 40-13 Tennessee win. LSU has won five of the last six, going back to 2005. How To Watch LSU vs Tennessee Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Neyland Stadium, Knoxville, TN – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why LSU Will Win The talent is still there, the coaching is still great, and now the pressure is off. LSU isn't going anywhere this season, and now it can be Lane Unleashed as the team throws everything at a Vols team with all of the weight on its side of the field. The defense is the best in the SEC, the offense is the best in the SEC, the team holds the ball longer than anyone else in the conference, and no one in America generates more sacks. Tennessee has a problem keeping defenses out of the backfield, and now, here come the Tigers. Why Tennessee Will Win LSU might generate the most sacks in America, but Tennessee can bring the heat, too – the Tigers are No. 2 in sacks. It didn't sack Marcel Reed in last week's 22-7 win over Texas A&M, but it gave him a rough time. Now the Vols are back at home, where they take their defensive production up several notches. The defense has allowed just one touchdown pass in five games in Neyland, but in this, it's about the Tennessee run defense. LSU is 1-3 when running for fewer than 140 yards. Auburn and Furman – the Vols called off the dogs against the Paladins – are the only teams to hit the 140-yard mark. LSU vs Tennessee Prediction, Betting Lines Here's the thing about LSU this season. It pounces on the weak, but its best win is … at Auburn? That's good, but there really isn't a second-best victory going 0-4 against the current CFP-ranked teams on the slate. Tennessee is a top team. This might not be the sexiest team going, but it's got grit. It's a tough defensive team that doesn't make a ton of mistakes, and it doesn't get rattled. LSU will be terrific, but like the Kentucky and Texas games, it'll crumble late in the final moments. Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Saul Young/News Sentinel Zach Ragan · AtoZ Sports Thu, November 19, 2026 at 2:56 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Volunteers are in a must-win situation this week against the LSU Tigers. The Tennessee Vols need a win against the LSU Tigers this weekend to remain in the College Football Playoff picture. It's possible that Tennessee could still make the playoff with a third loss, but they'd definitely be on the bubble. The only way to leave no doubt is to win out. LSU, meanwhile, is playing for nothing more than pride after suffering their fourth loss of the season last week against the Texas Longhorns. How much pride will LSU have when they come to Knoxville on Saturday? Tennessee has a 59% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 4% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). That's the big question that Fox Sports' Joel Klatt had this week while making his prediction for the game. "You get this transactional LSU bunch coming in with four losses," said Klatt. "Who knows what you're going to get from LSU. I have no idea. They're talented. They could play really well in this game. I wouldn't bet against it. It's still a team that played well against Bama and had chances to win that game before making too many mistakes. They certainly could have beaten Texas last week in that game. They give up the touchdown with two seconds to go and lose by one. "What do we get from (LSU QB) Sam Leavitt? I don't know. Their fan base is big mad about him not singing the alma mater, and then he's asked about it, and he's like, 'I'm not on social media,' and he gives this answer that's not going to cool anybody's animus. It's a transactional team. Can that work? Yes, it can work. Is it working here? No, it's not working. So, what type of motivation does that group have to play well in this game? I don't know. I think it is a complete unknown. Leavitt has 13 picks on the season. Last week, those three really cost them. Are the [LSU players] thinking about the NFL? You bring in guys that are transactional, what are they playing for? What is their why? I don't know. I know what Tennessee's why is, and I know how they're going to try to win the game — run game defense. I'm going to trust that." Klatt is taking Tennessee to win the game 24-21. "Neyland is going to be on fire," said Klatt. "They have not forgotten about Lane Kiffin. I'm going with Tennessee winning this one. They are actually getting a point and a half. I don't quite understand that, but they're getting a point and a half. I'll take it. I'll even make it a close game. Tennessee 24-21." Tennessee and LSU will kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.blurb: LSU trending to return another defender who had been out since spring with an injury By JON BLAU | Staff writer Jon Blau A week after LSU returned defensive end Gabriel Reliford from a spring ACL tear, the Tigers will return another defender from a nearly season-ending injury. Sophomore cornerback Aidan Anding , who tore his Achilles tendon in the spring, was listed as “probable” in the Southeastern Conference’s Thursday availability report for the LSU-Tennessee contest. Linebacker Whit Weeks, who was listed as “doubtful” in Wednesday’s report, was ruled out in Thursday’s edition, while receivers Jackson Harris and Winston Watkins remained “questionable” heading into Saturday’s 2:30 p.m. kickoff. However, the Vols are still competing for a spot and LSU can spoil Tennessee's season with a victory in Knoxville. This article originally appeared on LSU Wire: LSU football star wide receiver questionable for Tennessee game If Harris can't go, LSU is without its top offensive weapon against one of the SEC's top defenses. Harris has caught 55 passes for 864 yards and nine touchdowns. Harris transferred to LSU after a productive year with Hawai'i, and his emergence at LSU has put him in the conversation as a potential first-round draft pick in 2027. Harris is a complete player, winning contested catches on the outside and making plays with the ball in his hands. Harris has found a new gear over the last month, racking up 493 yards over LSU's last four games.

home.headline: LSU vs Tennessee: What is LSU's all-time record vs the Vols?
home.blurb: Saturday's tilt marks the first between the two sides since 2022. Tennessee came away with a 40-13 victory in Baton Rouge. Before that, the Volunteers' last win came in 2005, with a 30-27 overtime win inside Tiger Stadium. The rest of the stretch belongs to the Tigers. In between the 2005 and 2022 matches, LSU won five-straight games against Tennessee. The two most recent victories came on the road in 2011 and 2017. The purple and gold won both contests by 20 or more points. Tennessee ranks No. 9 in the most recent US LBM poll. The Volunteers are jostling for position in the College Football Playoffs while the Tigers are looking to end the first season under Kiffin with their first top-10 win of the season. After being listed as questionable every day leading in to their game against Texas, Whit Weeks is listed as doubtful this week. He dressed out fully and participated in warmups, but did not play a snap. Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports has reported that not only is the senior linebacker expected to miss Saturday’s contest, but it’s looking more likely that he’s done for the season. The other notable news for LSU is wide receivers Jackson Harris and Winnie Watkins being listed as questionable. We’ve seen Harris come up hobbled a few times over the past few games, but he’s shown grit and toughness and returns to the field. It is unclear what his specific injury is. Jhase Thomas being listed as probable likely means that he is expected to play, but did not practice fully on Wednesday. As for Tennessee, they have 10 players listed as out. The big news, though, is that quarterback George MacIntyre is not listed. He left their game last weekend against Texas A&M in the 3rd quarter with a knee injury and did not return. After taking over for Faizon Brandon as the Volunteers starting QB, MacIntyre is 4-1 and has helped them reach the top-10 in the College Football Playoff rankings. Tennessee comes in to Saturday’s contest ranked #9 and 8-2, while LSU fell out of the rankings following last week’s last second loss to Texas that dropped them to 6-4. Miami is clearly getting into it with an unblemished ACC record, along with only two weeks remaining. The Hurricanes got past Duke last weekend and the Virginia Tech game this weekend doesn't appear as difficult as it did a few weeks ago. Wake Forest is also in the driver's seat. Last weekend, the Demon Deacons crushed SMU in a game that likely determined who would face the Hurricanes. But SMU has a chance to right a few wrongs this weekend, and play spoiler , traveling to South Bend to play Notre Dame. Here's how the ACC games might play out this weekend. Kevin Jennings has already thrown for more than 2,900 yards this season and there are playmakers all over the field for Rhett Lashlee's team. But SMU has the second-most turnovers in the ACC, giving the ball up 15 times in 10 games. That's not winning football, and playing against a team like Notre Dame, with a veteran quarterback like CJ Carr, won't win you that game. SMU was thrashed against Wake Forest last weekend, and it was due to too many mistakes and the defense not stopping Gio Lopez. Carr has just two interceptions this season and if Jennings and Co. make mistakes, the Irish could turn the rout on. Notre Dame should be able to run the football against the Mustangs, too. The only way this game is close is if SMU scores quickly and gains some confidence and belief that it can win this game. picks.headline: Notre Dame vs SMU Final Score Prediction: Can the Fighting Irish make a statement against the Mustangs on Senior Day?
picks.blurb: Notre Dame vs SMU Final Score Prediction: Can the Fighting Irish make a statement against the Mustangs on Senior Day? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games TNF preview: Texans have hope? Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Notre Dame vs SMU score prediction Ryan Roberts · AtoZ Sports Thu, November 19, 2026 at 2:40 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Notre Dame football hosts SMU in its final home game of the 2026 regular season. What should Fighting Irish fans expect in South Bend? Notre Dame football is two wins away from a College Football Playoff berth. The Fighting Irish host the SMU Mustangs at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday in Notre Dame Stadium , and head coach Marcus Freeman's group needs to take care of business against SMU and then Syracuse to finish 11-1. It is also Senior Day. Hopefully the Irish land a home game in the playoff. Even so, this could be the last time this senior class walks out of the tunnel, hits the Play Like a Champion Today sign, and plays in front of the Notre Dame crowd. At one point, SMU looked like it would give Notre Dame's resume a nice bump. That changed after Wake Forest throttled the Mustangs last weekend. SMU trailed 42-0 at halftime and lost 49-7. This won't be the top-25 resume boost many expected, but Notre Dame still has plenty to play for. A decisive win could push the Irish up a couple more spots as the season winds down. Notre Dame has a 99% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 16% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). Notre Dame is a 90% favorite to win outright in the Kalshi prediction market. The Irish are favored by 20.5 points, which is roughly three touchdowns, and Kalshi gives them a 51% chance of covering that number. I like both, and I especially like Notre Dame to cover. Don't expect a Senior Day hangover Some people will look at this game and point to Senior Day, a potential hangover, and the other usual distractions. I just find it unlikely that Notre Dame won't be locked in and ready to play. We had the same conversation heading into the Boston College game after the Irish beat No. 1 Miami. Notre Dame was cool, calm, and collected, and the team was ready early. Slow first halves have popped up occasionally during Freeman's tenure, but we didn't see one last week. SMU is also substantially better than Boston College. I don't want anyone to underrate the Mustangs because of the Wake Forest result. That game was a bit of an anomaly. This is still a quality 7-3 team, and if SMU had been on a bye last week, we would feel a whole lot different about this matchup. Should Notre Dame win convincingly? Absolutely. Can the Irish show up with their C or D game and cruise? I don't think so. Kevin Jennings and the SMU passing game SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings has been really good outside of a couple of bad games. He is one of the better passers in college football and has developed steadily over the last couple of years. He has some dual-threat ability, but he wants to stay inside of structure and win from the pocket. I don't think Jennings is going to have back-to-back stinkers. SMU has some good receivers on the outside, including Jaylen Cooper. Notre Dame fans may remember Cooper from the 2025 recruiting class, when the Irish tried to flip him from SMU. The Notre Dame secondary will be tested. The Irish are still without DJ McKinney, but will have Jayden Sanders and Leonard Moore available. There are obviously good pieces on the back end, but the Mustangs have the potential to create a couple of explosive plays in the passing game. What keeps SMU from scoring a ton of points is the run game. It has been wildly inconsistent. The Mustangs have run for 250 yards in some games and fewer than 100 in others. An offense that isn't balanced will struggle to sustain drives against a defense this good, and SMU's feast-or-famine passing attack figures to be spotty. What to watch from the Notre Dame offense SMU's offense can be dangerous, but its defense is not good. That gives Notre Dame a chance to keep building on what has been working. I want to see the run game continue to ascend, so keep riding Nolan James Jr. and Jonaz Walton . Quarterback CJ Carr can add a few more explosives through the air and play a little more consistently. The bigger thing I'll be watching is how Notre Dame starts each half. The Irish have gotten off to fast starts more consistently recently, and that needs to continue. Against Boston College, Notre Dame put up a 24-point second quarter, then opened the second half with an interception. Winning those middle eights and coming out of the locker room with some juice is another massive key. Notre Dame vs. SMU score prediction I expect SMU to score some points, but 17 feels like about the best the Mustangs can do without a sudden breakthrough in the run game. I think Notre Dame starts to take control somewhere in the second quarter and stays in command throughout the second half. Final score prediction: Notre Dame 41, SMU 17 That covers the spread and gives the Irish the decisive victory they need. If they handle business on Saturday, only Syracuse stands between Notre Dame and a playoff berth. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.blurb: Notre Dame Opponent Preview: SMU Mustangs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games TNF preview: Texans have hope? Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Story by Roundtable Sports Notre Dame Opponent Preview: SMU Mustangs (Jerome Miron, USA TODAY Sports) Trevor Trowbridge · Roundtable Sports Tue, November 17, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time since 1989, the Notre Dame Fighting Irish will host the SMU Mustangs inside of Notre Dame Stadium. Their last meeting didn't go too well for the visiting Mustangs as the Irish won 59-6 and took their foot off the gas relatively early in the second half. This year, however, it's a different looking SMU team that travels up north. This program is two years removed from playing for the ACC title and making the first ever 12-team College Football Playoffs. They have talent littered all over the field and will look to play spoiler to Notre Dame's Senior Day and their College Football Playoff hopes. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET TV : NBC/Peacock Line : Notre Dame -20.5; O/U 56.5 Let's kick off our preview of this matchup with an overview look at the SMU Mustangs Record at SMU : 45-19 (5th season) SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee is in the midst of his fifth season at the helm. Like the coach he's facing this Saturday, Marcus Freeman , he has had a winning record in every season he's been the head coach. In 2023 and 2024, the Mustangs posted back to back 11-3 seasons, playing for the ACC title in 2024 and making the College Football Playoffs. Unfortunately, they lost soundly on the road against Penn State but that didn't take away from the great season he had. Last year, expectations were at an all-time high for Lashlee and SMU and they entered as one of the favorites to win the league. Unfortunately, they ended their season at 9-4 and weren't able to handle business down the stretch to get back to the ACC title game. This year, SMU is looking similar to the 2025 version of themselves rather than the 2023 and 2024 versions, but a win over Notre Dame in South Bend could drastically change the outlook of their season. Lashlee has the talent to compete with some of the top teams in the country at certain spots, but he needs to put it all together to make it back to the CFP which likely won't happen this season. Offensive Coordinator : Rob Likens / Garin Justice / D'Eriq King Defensive Coordinator : Maurice Crum Jr . / Rickey Hunley Jr . 2026 STATISTICAL OVERVIEW STATISTICAL LEADERS Rushing : RB Kendrick Raphael - 165 att., 809 yards, 4.9 YPC, 10 TD; RB Christian Rhodes - 23 att., 171 yards, 7.4 YPC, 2 TD; RB Dramekco Green - 43 att., 152 yards, 3.5 YPC, 1 TD; QB Kevin Jennings - 68 att., 127 yards, 1.9 YPC, 2 TD Passing : QB Kevin Jennings - 231-318, 72.6%, 2,973 yards, 9.3 YPA, 26 TD, 7 INT, 173.3 Rating; QB Ty Hawkins - 12-14, 85.7%, 117 yards, 8.4 YPA, 2 TD; 203.4 Rating Receiving : WR Yamir Knight - 55 rec., 670 yards, 12.2 YPC, 6 TD; WR Yannick Smith - 34 rec., 540 yards, 15.9 YPC, 3 TD; WR Jalen Cooper - 34 rec., 498 yards, 14.6 YPC, 2 TD; TE Randy Pittman Jr. - 30 rec., 312 yards, 10.4 YPC, 4 TD; WR Jalen Hale - 19 rec., 272 yards, 14.3 YPC, 3 TD; TE Theo Melin Ohrstrom - 18 rec., 217 yards, 12.1 YPC, 4 TD; WR Derrick McFall - 9 rec., 167 yards, 18.6 YPC, 3 TD; RB Kendrick Raphael - 16 rec., 138 yards, 8.6 YPC, 1 TD Tackles : LB Alexander Kilgore - 57; LB Brandon Booker - 48; S Jimmy Wyrick - 45; S Sael Reyes - 44; S Tyren Polley Jr. - 34; CB Jayvon Thomas - 32; NB Jarvis Lee - 30; DE Marques White - 28; LB Jamal Anderson - 28; CB Marcellus Barnes - 26; LB Brandon Miyazono Tackles For Loss : DE Marques White - 12.0; NB Jarvis Lee - 6.5; DE Aakil Washington - 5.0; DT Christian Davis - 4.5; LB Brandon Booker - 4.0; LB Alexander Kilgore - 3.5; S Sael Reyes - 3.5; DT Malcolm Alcorn-Crowder - 3.0; LB Brandon Miyazono - 3.0; S Tyren Polley Jr. - 3.0 Interceptions : NB Jarvis Lee - 1; LB Brandon Booker - 1; S Jimmy Wyrick - 1 The talent that SMU has on their roster doesn't match their output over the last two seasons. After going a combined 22-6 from 2023 through 2024, they're now 16-7 from the start of 2025 through Week 11 of this year's college football season. Quarterback Kevin Jennings returned for his final year at the helm. In some ways, he's having the season many thought he would, but his abilities as a runner have not been utilized by the offensive coaching staff. To a degree, it's understandable given the talent on the perimeter with players like Yamir Knight , Jalen Cooper , Yannick Smith , Jalen Hale , Theo Melin Ohrstrom and Randy Pittman Jr. requiring a lot of touches. Their defense has been the area of struggle this season, as it was last season. In many areas, Maurice Crum Jr ., a former Notre Dame captain at linebacker, has changed the outlook of the defense for the better. But they're a 'feast or famine' type of unit ranking 13th in the country in tackles for loss and 20th in the country in sacks but also ranking 110th in the country in passing touchdowns allowed and 128th in the country in red zone scoring allowed. This season, when they've faced offenses that can score, they've allowed 41 points to Louisville, 30 points to Syracuse and 49 points to Wake Forest. Can the Irish show up with their C or D game and cruise? I don't think so. Kevin Jennings and the SMU passing game SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings has been really good outside of a couple of bad games. He is one of the better passers in college football and has developed steadily over the last couple of years. He has some dual-threat ability, but he wants to stay inside of structure and win from the pocket. I don't think Jennings is going to have back-to-back stinkers. SMU has some good receivers on the outside, including Jaylen Cooper. Notre Dame fans may remember Cooper from the 2025 recruiting class, when the Irish tried to flip him from SMU. The Notre Dame secondary will be tested. The Irish are still without DJ McKinney, but will have Jayden Sanders and Leonard Moore available. There are obviously good pieces on the back end, but the Mustangs have the potential to create a couple of explosive plays in the passing game. What keeps SMU from scoring a ton of points is the run game. It has been wildly inconsistent. The Mustangs have run for 250 yards in some games and fewer than 100 in others. An offense that isn't balanced will struggle to sustain drives against a defense this good, and SMU's feast-or-famine passing attack figures to be spotty. What to watch from the Notre Dame offense SMU's offense can be dangerous, but its defense is not good. That gives Notre Dame a chance to keep building on what has been working. I want to see the run game continue to ascend, so keep riding Nolan James Jr. and Jonaz Walton . Quarterback CJ Carr can add a few more explosives through the air and play a little more consistently. The bigger thing I'll be watching is how Notre Dame starts each half. The Irish have gotten off to fast starts more consistently recently, and that needs to continue. Against Boston College, Notre Dame put up a 24-point second quarter, then opened the second half with an interception. Winning those middle eights and coming out of the locker room with some juice is another massive key. Notre Dame vs. SMU score prediction I expect SMU to score some points, but 17 feels like about the best the Mustangs can do without a sudden breakthrough in the run game. I think Notre Dame starts to take control somewhere in the second quarter and stays in command throughout the second half. Final score prediction: Notre Dame 41, SMU 17 That covers the spread and gives the Irish the decisive victory they need. If they handle business on Saturday, only Syracuse stands between Notre Dame and a playoff berth. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 12 Preview: SMU Mustangs @ Notre Dame Fighting Irish | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 20, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC SMU has responded to losses with excellent poise. However, a trip to South Bend is a tough order. Time and date: Saturday, November 21 at 7:30 p.m. ET Location: Notre Dame Stadium — South Bend, IN Spread: Notre Dame (-20.5) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: Notre Dame leads, 10-3 Last meeting: Notre Dame 59, SMU 6 — November 11, 1989 Current streak: Notre Dame, 3 (1986-89) Setting the scene How does SMU respond to a loss? Especially a rare home defeat in which the Mustangs trailed 42-0 at halftime and effectively watched their ACC championship aspirations evaporate? The Mustangs have responded with tremendous poise under head coach Rhett Lashlee, who has not dropped consecutive regular season matchups since his inaugural campaign in 2022. But this isn’t just any follow-up matchup. Immediately after facing 9-1 Wake Forest, SMU must travel to South Bend and take on another 9-1 opponent in Notre Dame. SMU just suffered its first regular season defeat without holding a second half lead since 2023. Now, the Mustangs enter Saturday’s matchup as three-touchdown underdogs against one of the nation’s premier programs. A chance to deliver the ultimate bounce-back statement awaits at Notre Dame Stadium. SMU Mustangs outlook Last Saturday, SMU (7-3, 5-3 ACC) endured a series of unwanted firsts. The Mustangs lost their first-ever ACC matchup at home. The Mustangs suffered their first-ever home loss in ACC play and their first conference defeat by more than 10 points, falling 49-7 to Wake Forest after an uncompetitive first half. The road to redemption won’t get any easier against Notre Dame. However, the potential reward is even greater than last week’s setback, as SMU can secure its first victory over an AP Top 5 opponent since defeating No. 2 Texas in 1980. Program icon Kevin Jennings looks to author a signature performance before exhausting his eligibility. The fifth-year senior quarterback ranks seventh nationally in passing yards, sitting 27 yards shy of his third-straight 3,000-yard season. He’s also fifth in the country with 26 passing touchdowns. Most impressively, Jennings operates with some of the highest efficiency in the FBS. His 62.9 completion rate last week was his lowest of the season, and he ranks third nationally, connecting on 72.6 percent of attempts. SMU’s 15th-ranked offense can be as dynamic and explosive as any in the country, but that was not the case last week when it registered just 47 yards across its first six possessions. Wake Forest largely eliminated the Mustangs’ run game from the onset, forced early turnovers, and provided significant pressure on dropbacks. Part of the challenge has been integrating a revamped offensive line. SMU recently inserted two true freshmen into starting roles on the left side while retaining veterans Joshua Bates, Addison Nichols (who is questionable), and PJ Williams at center, right guard, and right tackle, respectively. That unit faces a formidable test against Notre Dame’s defensive front. The Mustangs’ rushing attack has been volatile this season. Starting running back Kendrick Raphael has eclipsed 100 yards three times in ACC play, but there were three other conference games where the entire ground game was held below 70 yards, including last week. Raphael remains the workhorse tailback, but freshman Christian Rhodes has gotten increasingly involved, generating 92 rushing yards two weeks ago against Virginia Tech. SMU features an abundance of capable playmakers in its receiving corps. Four Mustangs have at least 30 receptions on the season, led by Yamir Knight’s 56 catches for 670 yards and six touchdowns. Yannick Smith and Jalen Cooper are among other downfield threats, while tight end Randy Pittman Jr. has been a consistent intermediate target all season. This group supplies much of the offense’s explosive potential, helping SMU rank fifth nationally with seven 50+ yard completions this season. The Mustangs only surrendered more than 30 points once before last week. The defensive line had proven overwhelming against several ACC opponents, but Wake Forest managed to neutralize that advantage. SMU ranks 20th nationally and third in the conference with 2.8 sacks per game, spearheaded by Marques White. The eighth-year senior defensive end leads all ACC defenders with 8.5 sacks, while adding 12.0 tackles for loss, two forced fumbles, and two fumble recoveries in a standout season. SMU struggled containing the run game last week, and the defense has been middle-of-the-road in that department this year. The passing defense, meanwhile, has made significant strides since 2025, although it recently experienced a major setback. Safety Jimmy Wyrick is out for the year, joining Tyren Polley Jr. as the second starting safety to suffer a season-ending injury. However, reigning First Team All-ACC selection Ahmaad Moses, who was granted an injunction for temporary eligibility, will make his second appearance of the season after debuting against Wake Forest. Moses had five interceptions last year, including two against SMU’s most recent top-10 opponent, Miami (FL). As heavy road underdogs at Notre Dame, SMU can’t just rely on stops. The Mustangs need to ramp up their turnover output after producing just three interceptions in their first 10 games. Notre Dame Fighting Irish outlook Notre Dame (9-1, Independent) is continuing its College Football Playoff pursuit after missing the field in 2025. The Fighting Irish secured a signature win Nov. 7 against otherwise-undefeated Miami (FL), staving off a late comeback to put themselves in prime playoff position. Outside of close finishes against current top-10 opponents Miami (FL) and BYU, the Fighting Irish have demolished the competition. Their other eight victories all came by double-digits, and North Carolina was the only other opponent to finish within 17 points. Following off a 34-point annihilation of Boston College, Notre Dame currently ranks first in point differential against FBS opponents at +25.6 per game. Quarterback CJ Carr enjoyed a promising debut season last year, but the junior has taken another significant step forward in 2026. His completion percentage has ballooned to 67.9, his passing yards per game output has climbed by 10, and he has delivered an efficient 24 touchdowns against two interceptions. Given the lopsided nature of most Notre Dame games, the quarterback hasn’t been shouldered with a heavy load in second halves. But when he needed to come through against Miami (FL), he did with a season-high 319 passing yards along with three touchdowns. Carr is supported by the wide receiver duo of Jordan Faison and Micah Gilbert, who are nearly identical in production this season. Faison has 615 receiving yards and six touchdowns, while Gilbert presents 614 yards and six scores. Recently, Gilbert has taken command of the offense, recording 14 receptions for 184 yards and three touchdowns across his last two starts. That doesn’t mean Faison has faded into the background, and he found the end zone in both of those ACC victories. Replicating last year’s run game was never going to be easy after losing two first-round NFL Draft picks, but the Fighting Irish are steadily reestablishing an identity on the ground. They produced a 100-yard rusher in four of their last six outings. Much like the receiving corps, the running back room is driven by a duo with similar statistics and similar builds. Jonaz Walton has 655 rushing yards on the season, and he’s been the more explosive with 7.0 yards per carry. Meanwhile, Nolan James Jr. follows closely with 644 rushing yards, and his 10 touchdowns are tied for 18th in the country. But the underlying catalyst for Carr and the run game’s success is arguably the best offensive line in the country. Notre Dame ranks first nationally in fewest sacks allowed, surrendering just three through 10 games. The line, anchored by potential All-American gaurd Anthonie Knapp, has also surrendered the fewest tackles for loss and yardage from tackles for loss in the FBS. As dominant as Notre Dame’s seventh-ranked scoring offense has been, its fifth-ranked scoring defense has been equally as imposing. The Fighting Irish surrender just 13.8 points per game and lead the FBS in total defense, allowing a mere 240 yards per contest. Only three teams managed more to score more than 13 points against this unit — BYU (28), North Carolina (26), and Miami (FL) (24). Although Notre Dame hasn’t generated sacks at the highest rate, its defensive front has consistently disrupted opposing quarterbacks. Defensive end Boubacar Traore leads the charge with 5.0 sacks, 8.0 tackles for loss, and three forced fumbles, while his counterpart Bryce Young has registered 4.0 sacks and 6.5 tackles for loss. The Fighting Irish will be shorthanded at the next level, however, as inside linebacker Drayk Bowen remains out for the third-straight game. Rounding out an imposing defense is reigning unanimous All-American cornerback Leonard Moore. After intercepting five passes last season, Moore has yet to record a pick in 2026. That doesn’t mean opposing quarterbacks have found success targeting him. Rather, his presence has deterred passers from looking in his direction, and he has done a standup job locking up WR1s all season. Even against one of the highest-ranked opponents on the road, it is nearly impossible for things to go worse for SMU than they did last week. The Mustangs should enter South Bend with renewed urgency and considerably more competitiveness on both sides of the ball, keeping the matchup within reach through several quarters. Kevin Jennings is as great of a passer as Notre Dame will face this season, alsongside with Darian Mensah. SMU possesses enough offensive firepower to become just the fourth team to surpass 13 points against this remarkably stingy defense. However, the Mustangs will need to find production in multiple areas to remain competitive. Notre Dame holds significant advantages elsewhere, particularly in the trenches. The Fighting Irish’s dominant offensive line should provide CJ Carr ample time to survey SMU’s secondary while opening running lanes for a backfield that has become increasingly productive as of late. That combination could prove overwhelming for a Mustangs defense that surrendered 49 points last week. SMU will put up a much better fight than it did against Wake Forest, but Notre Dame’s physicality will take over. The Fighting Irish withstand one of their tougher tests and continue the trek toward their fourth CFP appearance since 2018. all that stands between the Irish and the 12-team playoff field is SMU (7-3) and Syracuse (5-5). The Irish welcome SMU to South Bend for the regular season home finale, and that’s after SMU was destroyed on senior day by Wake Forest, 49-7. The Irish will have their senior day versus SMU, so the Mustangs have the chance to be party crashers. However, if there’s any inclination to quit a second straight week after falling behind early, then SMU will get blown out again. After SMU went for it on fourth down back-to-back possessions in their own territory and failed to convert, you could see the quit. SMU turned the ball over three times, went 3-of-14 on third downs, and gave up 535 yards of offense. Notre Dame had 500 yards of offense against Boston College, with 276 of it coming on the ground. The Irish ran for 6.9 yards a pop as Jonaz Walton led the way with 141 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Micah Gilbert and Jordan Faison have both scored back-to-back games (Gilbert three-straight), and CJ Carr had his ninth game with at least 200 passing yards and eighth with two-plus touchdown passes. The defense held Boston College to a season-low 136 yards of offense, nine first downs, and 2-of-18 on third and fourth downs. Oddsmakers peg Notre Dame as a -20.5 point favorite, and after what happened to SMU last week, the Irish could very well blow the Mustangs out too. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. CJ Carr has seven touchdowns to one pick in that span and averaged 248.6 passing yards per game, completing 70.1% of his passes (68/97). Nolan James Jr. has four rushing touchdowns in that span and is averaging 81.3 rushing yards per game, while Jonaz Walton registered 76.3 rushing yards per game and two scores. Jordan Faison and Micah Gilbert have scored back-to-back games as the Irish have been rolling. On paper, it doesn’t look like SMU’s defense will stop the Notre Dame offense. Like Boston College, the Irish should probably be able to pick the number of points they want to score before bringing in the backups late. Notre Dame Player to Watch on Offense: QB CJ Carr CJ Carr had a great game against Boston College, but his third-quarter interception hurt his Heisman odds dramatically. Carr was cruising until that point and finished the game with 217 passing yards on 20-of-28 for two touchdowns and an interception. Carr has 23 passing touchdowns to two interceptions and 2,385 passing yards. He is poised to surpass his freshman numbers and also cut down on taking sacks tremendously. Carr took 12 sacks through 12 games last year, down to three sacks in 10 games. The Notre Dame Fighting Irish Defense: Notre Dame’s defense stifled Boston College, and despite the Eagles’ threatening to score a few times, the Irish shut the door, holding them to a combined 2-of-18 on third and fourth downs. The Irish held Boston College to 136 total yards, with 51 of that coming from the air for 2.1 yards per pass. The Irish dominated time of possession (35:52-24:28), and after scoring on its first three possessions, Notre Dame’s defense came up big with a sack-fumble that was scooped up for a touchdown. That was Notre Dame’s third defensive touchdown and the first since Week 4. Notre Dame Player to Watch on Defense: DL Boubacar Traore Boubacar Traore got back in the sack column against Boston College and forced a fumble. The big man has 5.0 sacks this year, which is just shy of his career-high 6.5 set last year. He has four of his five sacks at home, and all of his turnovers (3 FF, 1 INT). On the road, SMU has scored 27, 31, and 27 points, but is 1-2. SMU Player to Watch on Offense: QB Kevin Jennings It couldn’t get any worse on senior day than it did for Kevin Jennings. SMU’s offense found itself in a 14-0 first-quarter hole, then that became a 42-0 halftime deficit. Jennings took three sacks, threw an interception, and the offense fumbled twice. He finished with 209 yards on 22-of-35 passing in a negative game script, and will likely be trailing all game here for a second consecutive week. Jennings has 31 interceptions in the last three seasons with SMU and I’d expect another one or two picks added to that total in South Bend. The SMU Mustangs Defense: SMU’s defense has been an inconsistent unit, but one thing’s steady: when the Mustangs lose, they give up a lot of points. SMU has allowed 41, 30, and 49 points to Louisville, Syracuse, and Wake Forest in its three losses. On the road, SMU has given up 24, 31, and 30, so Notre Dame should be able to cross the 30-point mark too. SMU permitted Wake Forest to go 10-of-15 on third downs, 2-of-3 on fourth downs, rack up 23 first downs and 535 total yards of offense, including a hair short of 37 minutes of time of possession. That was also SMU’s first home loss in ACC play. I can’t imagine a bounce-back effort on the road from the Mustangs. SMU State Player to Watch on Defense: DE Marquise White Marquise White leads SMU with 8.5 sacks this season after posting five with the Mustangs last year. White had a sack against Wake Forest and has a sack in back-to-back games and in three of the last four. By Ryan Potts in College Football Published: November 16, 2026 at 9:49 am EST Notre Dame brings a three-game winning streak into its Week 12 home date with SMU. SMU needs a quick response after a lopsided home loss to Wake Forest. See my early SMU vs Notre Dame prediction and Week 12 pick below. The Notre Dame Fighting Irish (9-1) welcome the SMU Mustangs (7-3) to South Bend on Saturday, November 21, 2026, with kickoff set for 7:30 p.m. ET. Notre Dame has won three straight since a 28-24 loss at BYU, including a 31-24 win over Miami and a 41-7 rout of Boston College. SMU is 5-3 against ACC opponents but arrives off a 49-7 home loss to Wake Forest, the Mustangs' second loss in three weeks. My early SMU vs Notre Dame prediction hinges on a field goal's worth of margin. The Irish have already beaten two of their past three opponents by at least three touchdowns. Here's how the sportsbook spread compares with the price on that outcome. Jump to: Prediction | Spread and Odds | Week 12 Picks Early SMU vs Notre Dame Prediction Pick: Notre Dame to win by 21 or more points (50¢ on Kalshi ) My early SMU vs Notre Dame prediction is a comfortable Irish win by at least three touchdowns. CJ Carr has been efficient and careful, completing 197 of 290 passes for 2,385 yards, 23 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Jordan Faison leads Notre Dame with 49 catches for 615 yards and six touchdowns, while Jonaz Walton has 655 rushing yards and five scores. That balance should keep SMU guessing. Kevin Jennings has thrown for 2,973 yards and 26 touchdowns for SMU, but his seven interceptions give the Irish defense chances. Boubacar Traore leads Notre Dame with five sacks, and Luke Talich paces the unit with 47 tackles. The Mustangs can still score. Kendrick Raphael has 809 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns, and Yamir Knight leads the team with 670 receiving yards. Marques White's 8.5 sacks make him SMU's best bet to rattle Carr. away.headline: Notre Dame football regains two former starters for SMU week practice
away.blurb: SOUTH BEND — Brauntae Johnson, junior safety for Notre Dame football, was upgraded to questionable for Senior Night this week against Southern Methodist after missing nine full games due to left foot surgery. The Fort Wayne product, out since the first half of the season opener against Wisconsin, will return to practice on Tuesday and go from there. Johnson had hoped to make it back in time for the Miami game on Nov. 7, but his foot wasn’t close enough to 100% for that to happen. If it’s determined that he needs more practice time before facing an opponent, Johnson will be held out against the Mustangs and pointed toward the regular-season finale at Syracuse “This is the next phase of his progression in terms of return to play,” Freeman said. Left tackle Will Black is questionable with a concussion suffered after 27 offensive snaps against Boston College. Styles Prescod took over for the final 47 snaps without apparent issue. Defensive tackles Francis Brewu and Jason Onye remain questionable with knee injuries suffered in the first quarter against Navy on Halloween, but there’s finally some good news for hard-luck offensive lineman Charles Jagusah. Sixteen months after suffering a broken left humerus in a utility vehicle accident, the senior guard/tackle has been upgraded to questionable. Jagusah has undergone at least five surgical procedures as he deals with nerve damage in his upper arm, including a bone graft on March 18. “This is the next phase for him,” Freeman said. “That doesn’t mean he’ll go out there and start on Saturday, but that means he is actually practicing starting this week. That is huge. That’s amazing for that young man that has been through so much to be at the point now he can return to practice.” “He’s been training and rehabbing,” Irish coach Marcus Freeman said Monday Nov. 16. “We’re going to try to integrate him back into practice and see how his body responds. There are some football-specific movements that you do in practice that you can’t simulate in rehab.” Analysis: Play by play, Notre Dame football keeps it eyes on the prize Freeman noted the Rock Island, IL product has appeared in postseason games for the Irish, including the 2024 College Football Playoff semifinal and title games, but he’s yet to play a home game in college. “He’s never stepped on the field in a game at Notre Dame Stadium,” Freeman said. “If he can help us and we can find a role, how cool would that be to do that on Saturday? His journey has been amazing in terms of the things he’s overcome.” Senior offensive lineman Chris Terek, coming off right knee surgery in August, has been removed from the injury report as well. Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Our college football picks for Louisville-Pitt, Kentucky-Missouri, more Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome to Week 12 of The Courier Journal's college football picks! Kentucky football is headed to Missouri. Louisville will host Pitt. And Western Kentucky will play at Liberty. The other two games we'll predict are Miami-Virginia Tech and Tennessee-LSU. The Courier Journal's Week 12 College Football Picks Here's a look at this week's picks. As is our custom, predictions are straight-up winners and losers (not against the spread), with rankings based on the latest US LBM Coaches Poll . All times listed are ET, and all odds listed are per DraftKings as of Tuesday, Nov. 17. Pitt at No. 22 Louisville How to watch : Saturday, 7:30 p.m., ESPN2 The picks : Eight for Louisville Betting line : Louisville -14, over/under 50.5 points UofL is looking to end ACC play on a high note with a resounding win over Pitt at home. The Cardinals' offense was uncharacteristically limited against North Carolina last weekend. Louisville was averaging nearly 41 points per game before only scoring 16 in Chapel Hill. As our Alexis Cubit wrote in her preview story earlier this week, UofL needs to find its explosiveness again if it wants to beat a Pitt defense that ranks seventh in the ACC in points allowed during conference play (24.7). No. 18 Kentucky at Missouri How to watch : Saturday, 7:30 p.m., SEC Network The picks : Four for Kentucky, four for Missouri (Alexis Cubit, Alaina Morris, Jason Frakes, Payton Titus) Betting line : Missouri -5.5, over/under 48.5 points After a historically great start to the season, UK heads to Columbia, Missouri, this weekend, where it hopes to avoid a third consecutive loss. The Wildcats could use a pick-me-up before their annual rivalry game against the Cards next Saturday. But they might have a tough time against the Tigers , who've also dropped their past two contests and want to salvage a somewhat disappointing season. Western Kentucky at Liberty How to watch : Saturday, 1 p.m., ESPN+ The picks : Eight for Liberty Betting line : Liberty -17.5, over/under 53.5 points The Hilltoppers have their work cut out for them against the 9-1 Flames . Liberty is undefeated in Conference USA contests, while WKU is 3-3. Last weekend, Liberty defeated the Middle Tennessee team that beat WKU the week prior. Can the Hilltoppers pull off the improbable upset? Virginia Tech at No. 6 Miami How to watch : Saturday, 7 p.m., ESPN The picks : Eight for Miami Betting line : Miami -20.5, over/under 61.5 points The Hurricanes had a resounding win over the Duke Blue Devils last weekend, once again without their best player (wideout Malachi Toney), after suffering a heartbreaking loss to Notre Dame the week before. Virginia Tech, on the other hand, travels to South Florida after back-to-back failings against SMU and Stanford. Hence the massive advantage the bookies have bestowed upon Miami. ESPN's "College GameDay" will be there, though this sportswriter isn't sure why. Should be a cut-and-dry victory for the Hurricanes. Which hasn't meant much considering their 6-4 record. Fascinating that the oddsmakers still think highly enough of LSU to favor it on the road at Tennessee, of all places. picks.blurb: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games TNF preview: Texans have hope? Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Story by Wildcats Wire Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:25 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to CoMo for the final road game of the season against the Missouri Tigers. The Wildcats offense desperately needs to respond after scoring just 20 points in the last two weeks which has led to back-to-back losses. Missouri is a well coached, good all around football team and the defense has been consistent this season. However, the Tigers had their worst defensive performance of the season on the road last week against Georgia. Both teams are coming off back-to-back losses, Kentucky has scored just 20 points on offense in the past two weeks. Conversely, the Missouri defense has allowed 72 points over the last two weeks, albeit to Georgia and Texas. Kentucky has to find some of the offensive success they had before the bye week if they want to finish the season on a strong note. A win at Missouri would give the Wildcats six wins in SEC play, which has only happened once in program history and that was in the 1977 season. I fully expect a motivated performance from both teams to try and put an end to their respective two-game losing streaks. Kentucky's offensive line was named a semifinalist for the Joe Moore Award and have since had to of their worst performances of the season. Last week against Florida was the worst the offensive line has looked all season, so you can almost guarantee they will respond the right way in this game. Quiet frankly, they have to because if the offensive line plays like they did against the Gators they will be in danger of a winless month of November. Missouri's defense has playmakers at every level, but they will allow teams to move the football. Among SEC teams, the Tigers rank 10th in success rate allowed, 7th in pass success rate allowed and 12th in rush success rate allowed. Missouri also ranks 8th in the SEC in EPA/play allowed, 7th in EPA/pass allowed and 12th in EPA/rush allowed. The Tigers have also allowed explosive plays this season, as they rank 14th in the conference in explosive play rate allowed. This will be a difficult matchup for Kentucky, but it starts by winning the line of scrimmage and getting the run game going. The Wildcats averaged just two yards per carry against Florida and had just 61 rushing yards. They will lose this game if they can not turn that around, but the Missouri run defense has struggled at times this season. Kentucky has to stay ahead of the chains and that starts with the run game on early downs, which is something they had been good at all season. We mentioned the Tigers have playmakers at every level of the defense, and that starts up front with edge defender Daeden Hopkins. Hopkins leads the team in sacks (7) and tackles for loss (7.5). Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez leads the middle of the defense, Rodriguez is a tackling machine with a team-leading 107 tackles on the season; he also has seven tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks on the year. The secondary is led by safety Santana Banner, Banner has 84 tackles on the season, 6 pass breakups and 2.5 tackles for loss. Kentucky has to account for these three players, as they are the strength of this Missouri defense at every level. Hopkins, Rodriguez and Banner have each forced two fumbles this season as well. They have consistently made big time plays for the Tigers all season long. Kentucky has to find ways to exploit this defense and avoid letting these three players make game changing plays. In a lot of ways, this matchup is about Kentucky after scoring just 20 points in the last eight quarters. The offense just is not playing well, and what happened on the line of scrimmage against Florida was alarming. Kentucky has to get the big blue wall back to playing like semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. This offense lacks explosive plays and yards after contact ability, so they will continue to struggle if the offensive line can't get back to playing at a high level. Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers’ playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it “not a good plan offensively or defensively,” and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. When he gets protection he can pick you apart. RB Ahmad Hardy: A preseason AP First Team All-American and the engine of the run game. Kentucky’s run defense has to be better than it was against Florida. RB Jamal Roberts: The second back in a deep backfield. WR Donovan Olugbode: Simmons’ favorite target and the guy they go to on third down. OL Cayden Green: A preseason Second Team All-American who anchors the line. Keys to the Game Fix the run defense. Florida ran 48 times for 211 yards and wore Kentucky down in the second half. Missouri will try the exact same thing with Hardy. If Kentucky can’t set the edge, it’s going to be a long night. Get the run game going again. Kentucky’s offense works when the run sets up Kenny Minchey. Sixty-one rushing yards won’t win in the SEC, let alone on the road at night. Attack the secondary. Pass defense has been Missouri’s weak spot all year. Georgia’s Gunner Stockton went 18 of 24 for 252 yards. Minchey needs to take his shots. Start fast. Missouri has started slow on the road and on the ropes. Kentucky has led into the second half against Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida and lost all three. The second half is where this team has to grow up. Win the turnover battle. Kentucky’s big wins this year came down to a play here and there. Simmons has been careless with the ball against good defenses. Make him pay. Our Early Prediction This one comes down to which team handles adversity better. Both are coming off back-to-back losses, and both had playoff hopes that are now gone. Missouri has the home field and is favored by almost a touchdown. Kentucky has the head coach who has won close games all year. What gives me some hope is the bounce back. After Alabama blew them out, the Cats went on the road and beat Texas A&M. Stein has had a whole week to get this team’s attention after being called out for not looking like themselves. I think Kentucky responds. picks.headline: How No. 16 Kentucky football and Missouri match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.8% completions, 2,160 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. two interceptions) had a challenging game in UK’s 21-14 upset loss to visiting Florida last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound product of Hendersonville, Tennessee, completed only 15 of 26 passes for 181 yards with one touchdown. In going 0-2 since returning from an Oct. 31 open week, Kentucky has allowed too much pressure on its QB. Minchey has been sacked six times and hurried 10 times total in losses to Tennessee and Florida. • Missouri’s Austin Simmons (62.3% completions, 2,379 yards, 21 touchdowns vs. three interceptions) has thrown for seven combined touchdowns in Mizzou’s past three games. A 6-4, 220-pound product of Miami, Simmons has already started a game vs. UK. Playing last season for Ole Miss, Simmons made his first career road start at Kroger Field. The QB threw two early picks as Ole Miss fell behind 10-0. Simmons steadied, however, and threw for 235 yards and ran for 44 yards and a TD as the Rebels rallied to beat Kentucky 30-23. Advantage : Missouri Running backs • UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (562 yards, 5.3 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) caught a 5-yard touchdown pass in the loss vs. Florida but had a hard time on the ground vs. the Gators. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, rushed 8 times for 21 yards vs. his home-state school. Since missing the Oklahoma game due to injury, Baxter has subsequently carried 20 times for 78 yards in the three games. Third-year player Jason Patterson (495 yards, 6 yards a carry, three TDs) had 22 yards on five rushes vs. Florida and caught a pass for nine yards. • Missouri’s Jamal Roberts (1,133 yards, 5 yards a carry, nine touchdowns) is second in the SEC in rushing. A 6-foot, 216-pound St. Louis product, Roberts has run for 100 yards or more in five games this season, and has gone above 200 yards rushing in a game twice. Ahmad Hardy led the SEC in rushing in 2025, running for 1,649 yards and 16 touchdowns. However, the 5-10, 210-pound product of Oma, Mississippi, missed the first seven games this season as he recovered from being shot in the left leg May 10 while attending an outdoor concert in Laurel, Mississippi. Since returning three games ago, Hardy has carried 10 times for 41 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby (49 catches, 601 yards, three touchdowns) needs two catches and 29 receiving yards to shatter Barion Brown’s UK freshman marks (50 receptions, 628 receiving yards in 2022) for most catches and receiving yards in a season. Second-year player DJ Miller (26, 324, 1) caught four passes for 80 yards vs. Florida but also had a costly drop on UK’s final offensive possession of the game. • Missouri’s Cayden Lee is second in the SEC in receptions and first in the conference in receiving yards (879). A transfer from Ole Miss, the 5-11, 180-pound fourth-year player has caught at least five passes in every Mizzou game in 2026 other than last week’s 48-21 loss at No. 1 Georgia, when he was held to three receptions for 44 yards. Lee caught one pass for eight yards for Ole Miss in its win at Kentucky last season. Sophomore Donovan Olugbode is also having a big year for Missouri. The 6-2, 210-pound Chicago product has made 47 catches for 691 yards and eight touchdowns. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is tied for fifth in the FBS in receptions by a tight end with 50. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School has turned those team-high 50 receptions into 467 receiving yards and three touchdowns. A model of consistency, Rodriguez has caught either five or six passes in each of UK’s past six games. • Missouri’s Brett Norfleet has 14 catches for 120 yards and two TDs. The 6-6, 255-pound fourth-year player caught one pass for seven yards in last week’s loss to Georgia. Jude James has averaged 10 yards a catch on his seven receptions. Advantage : Kentucky Offensive line • In the losses to Tennessee and Florida the past two weeks, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has seemed to struggle in pass protection. Of the 6-8, 329-pound Madison Central product, Will Stein said “We all know, I know, (I) think everybody on our team knows (Wood’s) talent level is as good as you’re going to find in the country. It’s just consistency at that position.” • Missouri left tackle Cayden Green is the pillar of a Tigers offensive front that has surrendered the fewest QB sacks (nine) in the SEC. After starting five times for Oklahoma in 2023, Green transferred to Mizzou and started all 13 games in 2024 at left guard. Since switching to left tackle prior to the 2025 season, the 6-5, 324-pound Green has become a standout. So far in 2026, he has not allowed a sack or quarterback hit. Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (36 tackles, six sacks, nine tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) had a streak of three straight games with at least one sack snapped vs. Florida. Tackle Tavion Gadson (33 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries) also made four stops against the Gators. Gadson has now gone three games without a sack. • Missouri defensive end Daeden Hopkins is fourth in the SEC with seven sacks. The 6-6, 250-pound second-year player has also been credited with 11 quarterback hurries. A transfer from Miami, second-year tackle Donta Simpson has emerged as a disruptor for Eli Drinkwitz and Co. The 6-4, 300-pound Simpson has six QB sacks, 7.5 tackles for loss and eight QB hurries. Advantage : Even • Even though Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey (13 tackles) and WLB Bo Barnes (nine stops) were UK’s two leading tacklers vs. Florida, the prevailing thought was that UF’s ample success with the QB run game owed, in some part, to the Wildcats’ linebackers not fitting the run properly. “There were some big, big missed tackles in the game that sprung explosive runs by their quarterback,” Will Stein said. “That goes back to us not executing the fundamentals and technique of our position.” • Missouri WLB Nicholas Rodriguez leads the SEC in tackles with 107. The 6-foot, 225-pound Miami product has made at least 11 tackles in eight of Mizzou’s 10 games to date. MLB Robert Woodyard Jr ., a transfer from Auburn, is 22nd in the SEC with 64 tackles and has forced two fumbles and picked off a pass. Defensive backs • Kentucky safeties Jordan Castell and Ty Bryant are tied for second in the SEC in interceptions with four apiece. However, neither has a pick in either of UK’s past two games, the losses at Tennessee and to Florida. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound product of Orlando, is ninth in the SEC with 76 tackles. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Lexington native, is 12th in the SEC with 74 stops. • Missouri cornerbacks Sione Laulea and Chris Graves Jr. are tied for second in the SEC with 10 passes successfully defended. Strong safety Santana Banner has recovered two fumbles and broken up six passes. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 12 of 15 on field-goal tries with a long make of 52 yards. For the second time this season, UK switched punters vs. Florida. After Wilson Berry punted for four games (averaging 42.6 yards a kick), UK went back to its original starting punter of 2026, Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara , vs. the Gators. O’Hara kicked three times vs. UF and averaged 46.3 yards a kick. On the season, O’Hara, an Australian, has averaged 41.5 yards on 20 punts. • Missouri place-kicker Blake Craig has missed nine of his 24 field-goal tries this season but has a long make of 53 yards. Craig has been better from outside 50 yards (5 of 7, 71.4%) than from inside 50 yards (10 of 17, 58.8%). Punter Brunno Reus is averaging 44.47 yards a kick and has stopped 18 of 47 punts inside the opponent’s 20-yard line. Punt returner DaMarion Fowlkes averaged 10 yards a return and had a 68-yard TD vs. Troy. As a kickoff returner, Fowlkes is averaging 24.8 yards on 12 returns. Georgia football injury report vs. Missouri
All-SEC Georgia star's status in doubt vs. Missouri
home.blurb: However, Georgia has two new players that popped up on the injury report. Georgia starting center Drew Bobo, an All-SEC pick, is doubtful to play. It is unclear what Bobo's injury is, but if he misses the game, then that would be significant for the Georgia offensive line, which is coming off a dominant performance against Ole Miss. Georgia missed Bobo last year in the SEC championship and the postseason. He's a critical part of the Georgia offense. Up front, Georgia's Josh Horton is questionable. Horton is a new player listed on the injury report and has seven tackles and two sacks this season. Pass rusher Amaris Williams remains out for Georgia after tearing his ACL in spring practice. Georgia has some banged up players that aren't on the injury report. Running back Dante Dowdell remains out and running back Chauncey Bowens did not play against Ole Miss despite not having an injury designation. "He's not 100%," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said on Bowens. "Just because someone is dressed out and cleared does not mean that they're able to go out there and play and perform. He's working his tail off to get back." Out: Linebacker Amaris Williams (torn ACL) Out: Running back Dante Dowdell (upper body) Questionable: Defensive lineman Josh Horton Out: Offensive lineman Josh Atkins Missouri star quarterback Austin Simmons and receiver Cayden Lee do not appear on the Tigers' availability report. Both players needed medical assistance during the Missouri loss to Texas, but appear to be able to play against Georgia. away.blurb: Although there are no new Cal players listed as being out, four starters are listed as questionable. Starting wide receiver Ian Strong, who missed last week's game, as well as defensive back Daniel Harris, safety Isaiah Crosby and inside linebacker JD McKinley are the four Cal starters listed as questionable. Safety Aiden Manutai, outside linebacker Justin Beadles and defensive lineman Ashun Shepphard are also Cal players expected to get playing time if they are healthy, but all three are listed as questionable. Also of interest is the fact that quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and running back Adam Mohammed are listed as probable. That indicates they are likely to play against Stanford, but it also suggests they are nursing some injuries. Three Cal players listed as being out for the Big Game are the same players who have been sidelined for virtually the entire season -- running back Carter Vargas, defensive lineman Nate Burrell and tight end Dorian Thomas. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/cal as Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable . The initial injury report for Saturday's Cal-Stanford game was released Wednesday night, and a number of key Cal players are listed. Strong is the Bears' second-leading receiver with 35 catches for 478 yards, while McKinley, who also missed last week's game, is the team's co-leader in sacks with three. Crosby is second on the team in tackles with 56 and he also has an interception and two tackles for loss. Harris is fifth on the team in tackles with 37, and he also has three tackles for loss and four quarterback hurries. Cal is 3-7 overall and is riding a four-game losing streak. The Bears will host Stanford (5-5, 4-5 ACC) in Saturday's Big Game starting at 4:30 p.m. The Cardinal would become bowl-eligible if it beats Cal. The TCU Horned Frogs will face one of their toughest challenges of the season Saturday when they host No. 2 Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium. The Frogs are coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State , while the Utes enter the matchup looking to keep their undefeated season alive. Utah is 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big 12 play. Saturday's matchup will mark the highest-ranked opponent to visit Amon G. Carter Stadium since No. 2 Texas in 1970. It also marks TCU's final home game of the season before the Frogs travel to face Texas Tech on Thanksgiving Day. With a win, TCU would secure bowl eligibility and pull off one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. When TCU has the ball Quarterback Jaden Craig will be a key factor in TCU's ability to keep up with Utah's offense. Craig has thrown for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season. He is coming off a 225-yard performance against Kansas State, where he also threw a touchdown pass. The Horned Frogs will need to find ways to create offensive opportunities without relying entirely on Craig's arm. Establishing the run game and finding success on early downs will be important against a Utah defense that has helped the Utes remain undefeated. Craig has also been dealing with an ankle injury that has limited his mobility. However, head coach Sonny Dykes said during Tuesday's midweek news conference that Craig is showing improvement and is expected to play Saturday. "I would expect him to play. He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday," Dykes said Tuesday. His ability to make plays through the air will put pressure on TCU's secondary. TCU's defense will need to create pressure, limit big plays and force Utah into difficult third-down situations. If the Frogs cannot slow down Dampier and the Utes' offense, it could be a long night for the defense. This will be one of the toughest games of the season for the Horned Frogs. TCU is coming off a big win over Kansas State and will be hungry to prove it can compete with one of the best teams in the country. While I expect the Frogs to put up a fight, they have struggled to perform consistently under pressure this season. Utah has remained undefeated for a reason, and its strength on both sides of the ball will make this a difficult matchup for TCU. I expect the Horned Frogs to compete early, but Utah's consistency will ultimately be too much to overcome. The Horned Frogs are one win away from bowl eligibility, but they'll have to earn it against either Utah or Texas Tech in their final two games. Can Utah keep its perfect season alive, or will TCU deliver another Big 12 After Dark surprise? Here's everything you need to know about Utah vs. TCU, including betting odds, injury updates, the biggest question and our prediction. How does Devon Dampier, Wayshawn Parker/Daniel Bray handle the ground game, which they will want to get going on the road to stay undefeated? That's the biggest question of the game and will determine whether or not an upset might be in store. Utah vs. TCU Pick and Prediction TCU is 5-5, but every loss has been by one score. That's a testament to this defense, not so much the offense. They have the top scoring defense in the Big 12 this season, and rank second in total defense as well. But here's the thing, TCU's defensive numbers may be skewed in part by who they have, and haven't played, thus far this season. They wrap up the season playing Utah and Texas Tech, two of the more explosive offenses in the Big 12. And the other part of this that concerns me for TCU: Even if the defense holds its own, does it just get worn down as the game progresses, especially if TCU's offense can't get it going? TCU will and can put up an admirable fight, but I don't see it resulting in a win or a cover. Utah is 8-2 against the spread this year, and it'll be 9-2 come Saturday in Fort Worth. Utah football: Is it time for a change at punt returner? – Deseret News Deseret News Utah knows it has to improve in fielding punts as it hits the most important part of the schedule Utah’s special teams made huge strides in the team’s 40-39 win over Arizona. Kicker Dillon Curtis was 2-for-2 on field goals — including a 53-yard make — and 4-for-4 on extra points, including the go-ahead PAT in the fourth quarter. But a muffed punt by Mana Carvalho in the fourth quarter brought down the overall grade for special teams. Carvalho has had a number of close calls this season, and one finally went the wrong way for him against the Wildcats. The Utes, up by five, had just forced an Arizona punt with 10:27 left and were in position to possibly take a two-score lead with a successful offensive drive. Carvalho should have either fair caught the punt or let it go with Dwight Bootle II barreling down on him, but Carvalho tried to field it and muffed it, then got rocked by Bootle and had to be helped off the field and into the medical tent. Utah’s defense held strong as Arizona threatened in the red zone on the ensuing drive, forcing a field goal. Those saved four points would prove crucial in a one-point win. “We’ll know more by midweek. ... We think he’s going to be all right,” Scalley said. “You never know with that though. I don’t want to paint myself into a corner.” “Well, we’re always going to go off of what we see in practice and who’s catching it efficiently in practice,” Scalley said. Last year, under coach Kyle Whittingham, Carvalho fumbled a punt against BYU . He wasn’t benched, and a couple weeks later, returned a punt for a touchdown against Cincinnati. If Utah does make a change at punt returner, it will likely be to receiver Creed Whittemore, who has returned punts this season when Carvalho has gone to the sidelines injured.
